questions.q: The programming activities of a project were planned to last 35 days per module but the programming of the first module has taken 45 days. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the team to work overtime to complete the deliverable on time.
Evaluate the situation and identify ways to compress the schedule without impacting baselines.
Check the scope to verify if there is scope creep and get the project on schedule.
Submit a change request to the project sponsor to change the schedule.

questions.e: Evaluate and Identify Ways to Compress the Schedule: The project manager should first understand why the programming of the first module took longer than planned. This evaluation can help identify potential bottlenecks or inefficiencies. Schedule Compression: Techniques like fast-tracking (doing tasks in parallel that were originally planned in sequence) or crashing (adding resources to critical path tasks) can help compress the schedule without negatively impacting the project baselines (scope, cost, quality). Avoiding Scope Creep and Change Requests: Before considering scope changes or submitting change requests, it's essential to attempt schedule compression to bring the project back on track. This approach is less disruptive and maintains the integrity of the original project plan. This method ensures that the project manager addresses the delay proactively and seeks solutions that can keep the project within its original baselines.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a hybrid project. After attending an iteration review, a stakeholder tells the project manager that they are very busy and asks why these reviews are held so frequently. How should the project manager respond? *

o.t: Negotiate a reduced review attendance with the stakeholder and update the stakeholder engagement plan to reflect this reduced.
Discuss with the stakeholder the benefits of the hybrid project and how frequent reviews lead to greater value and less rework.
Record the issue in the issue log and escalate the conflict to the project sponsor for assistance.
Explain to the stakeholder that the stakeholder engagement plan requires their attendance at all reviews.

questions.e: Educating the Stakeholder: It's important to explain the value of frequent iteration reviews in a hybrid project. These reviews help ensure that the project stays on track, issues are identified early, and feedback is incorporated regularly, leading to better outcomes and less rework. Stakeholder Engagement: By understanding the benefits, the stakeholder may be more willing to participate, seeing the direct impact on the project's success and efficiency. Proactive Communication: This approach fosters a collaborative relationship and helps the stakeholder appreciate the importance of their involvement in the process.

questions.q: A large organization decided to adopt an agile methodology based on the trends seen in the industry. The organization invested a large amount of money in adopting it, but after a few months, the implementation failed. What should the project manager have done differently to avoid the implementation failure? *

o.t: Conducted agile training for all employees ranging from the project teams through mid-level to upper-level management.
Conducted a postmortem and captured the learning in organizational process assets (OPAs) for future use.
Assessed the organization's culture, performed a suitability analysis, and determined the future state.
Hired a third-party agile delivery team to do the implementation.

questions.e: Cultural Assessment and Suitability Analysis: Before adopting a new methodology like agile, it’s critical to assess whether the organization’s culture and existing processes are suitable for such a transition. This includes understanding the readiness of the organization, potential challenges, and how the current state compares to the desired agile state. Determining Future State: Defining a clear future state ensures that everyone understands the goals and how agile fits into the overall strategy. This helps in creating a structured and realistic plan for the transition. This approach ensures that the adoption of agile is aligned with the organization's culture and capabilities, thereby increasing the likelihood of successful implementation.

questions.q: A junior staff member was recently assigned to the team. The new team member tells the project manager that they are confused because they are not familiar with what is expected of them on the project. What should the project manager do to assist the new team member? *

o.t: Advise the new team member to enroll in project management training.
Instruct the new team member to review the responsible, accountable consult, and inform (RACI) matrix before asking for help.
Advise the new team member to review the project charter and stakeholder engagement plan.
Review the resource management plan and provide mentoring to the new team member if necessary.

questions.e: Resource Management Plan: This plan includes details on roles and responsibilities, training needs, and the onboarding process for new team members. Reviewing this plan helps the project manager understand the specific expectations and requirements for the new team member. Mentoring: Providing mentoring helps the new team member get up to speed quickly, clarifies expectations, and provides guidance on how to fulfill their role effectively. This personalized support can significantly improve their confidence and performance. By following these steps, the project manager ensures that the new team member receives the necessary support and clear guidance to integrate successfully into the team.

questions.q: A project is delayed due to multiple problems discovered during the quality review. Every time the team addresses one problem, additional problems are encountered. This is frustrating for both the project team and the project sponsor, who are driven to meet the dates and results expected by the organization. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Request that the team identifies, documents, and registers the issues to locate the source of the problems.
Evaluate the cost and schedule variance in order to determine how much the project is off track.
Ask the team to commit to a new date to fix all the problems and proceed with a change request to adjust the baseline.
Request that a senior subject matter expert (SME) be hired to analyze and solve the problems.

questions.e: Identifying and Documenting Issues: This step helps in understanding the root causes of the recurring problems. By documenting and registering the issues, the team can analyze patterns and potentially uncover underlying systemic issues that need to be addressed. Locating the Source of Problems: Finding the root cause is essential for implementing effective corrective actions and preventing similar issues in the future. This approach helps in developing a more comprehensive solution rather than just addressing symptoms. This proactive approach ensures that the project manager and the team can systematically address the problems, leading to a more sustainable resolution and minimizing future disruptions.

questions.q: A company has hired a vendor to deliver a scope of work and assigned a project manager to oversee the project. The vendor advised that they completed the scope successfully and is asking for approval. What should the project manager do in response to this request? *

o.t: Obtain approval from the project sponsor.
Update the project management plan and mark the milestone as completed.
Ask the vendor to validate the agreement for any deviations.
Set up a meeting with stakeholders to validate and confirm acceptance of the deliverables.

questions.e: Stakeholder Validation and Confirmation: It is important to validate and confirm that the deliverables meet the project requirements and stakeholder expectations before approving the vendor's work. Setting up a meeting with stakeholders ensures that all relevant parties review the completed work and confirm that it aligns with the agreed-upon scope and quality standards. Formal Acceptance: This step helps to ensure formal acceptance of the deliverables, reducing the risk of disputes or issues later on. It also provides a clear record of acceptance, which is essential for project documentation and closure. This approach ensures that the project manager follows a thorough and collaborative process for approving deliverables, maintaining transparency and stakeholder satisfaction.

questions.q: During project execution of a new IT solution, the testing of one feature was unsuccessful. The go-live milestone is now impacted due to this delay. Extensive analyses were performed, and there is no way to resolve the defects before the go-live date. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Include additional mitigation actions against feature defects and update the risk management plan.
Assess the relevance of the feature and then analyze the submission of a change request to descope it.
Improve the control quality process by implementing additional testing to minimize the defects before the go-live milestone.
Determine if business value will be delivered without this feature, and try to fix the defects after the go-live milestone.

questions.e: Since the testing of the feature was unsuccessful and cannot be resolved before the go-live milestone, the project manager must evaluate whether this feature is essential to the overall project success. If the feature is not critical or if there are alternative ways to deliver business value, then a change request should be considered to remove (descope) the feature. This ensures that the project can still meet its go-live date without unnecessary delays.

questions.q: The product team is progressing with a prototyping approach to deliver a multiyear business initiative. A few user stories are taking longer to be delivered. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Determine the risks and identify a resolution during the retrospective meeting.
Inform stakeholders about the delay during project updates.
Determine cross-dependencies and plan a spike in the next sprint.
Discover the gaps in the communications management plan and address them accordingly.

questions.e: When user stories are taking longer to be delivered, the project manager should analyze why and determine if there are cross-dependencies that may be causing the delay. A spike (a time-boxed research activity) in the next sprint can be planned to investigate technical challenges, test solutions, or gather more information to complete the stories efficiently. This approach aligns with Agile methodologies, where teams use spikes to resolve uncertainties or technical issues before continuing development.

questions.q: While preparing an earned value analysis (EVA) for the sponsor, the project manager provided this information in the latest project report: ✑ Approved Work Package Cost Estimates: US$9,500 ✑ Contingency reserves: $500 ✑ Management reserves: 10% of contingency reserves ✑ Percent complete of the project: 50% ✑ Planned percent of the project: 40% ✑ Actual costs of the project: US$4,500 What is accurate about the project status? *

o.t: The actual work is 25% more than the planned work.
The project cost is 10% lower than planned.
The actual work is 25% less than the planned work.
The project cost is 10% higher than planned.

questions.e: SPI= EV/PV = 1.25 This indicates the project is 25% ahead of schedule. ​The SPI of 1.25 indicates the project is performing 25% ahead of the planned schedule.

questions.q: After a project team has been working on a project for several months, the project is cancelled. The project sponsor is putting pressure on the project manager to perform closeout duties as fast as possible so that the project team can move on to other work. The project sponsor has instructed the team not to waste time archiving the project artifacts for the cancelled project. How should the project manager handle this situation? *

o.t: Comply with the project sponsor's request to not archive the project artifacts.
Document the project sponsor's instructions as the archived project artifacts.
Archive the project artifacts on the project manager's local computer for future reference.
Consult with the project management office (PMO) for guidance on project artifacts.

questions.e: Consulting with the PMO ensures that the project manager follows organizational policies and procedures regarding the handling and archiving of project artifacts. The PMO can provide guidance on what should be done in this situation, balancing the sponsor's request with the need for proper documentation and record-keeping. This approach ensures compliance with organizational standards and mitigates potential issues that could arise from not properly archiving project artifacts.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a project that is in development. As the project manager reviews the projects progress, they find a few tasks that are behind schedule. After investigating the project manager discovers that a few team members were pulled to work on other assignments, which impacted their ability to focus on the project manager’s project. Which two actions can the project manager take to bring the team back on track? (Choose two) *

o.t: Establish daily standups to review project progress and track the completion of deliverables.
Allow the team members to catch up at their own pace.
Alert the business stakeholders immediately of the schedule delay.
Discuss the risk of project delay and work priorities with the respective functional managers.
Work with the team to identify options to accelerate project delivery.

questions.e: D. Discuss the risk of project delay and work priorities with the respective functional managers: By discussing the situation with the functional managers, the project manager can address the allocation of resources and ensure that team members are available to focus on the project. This helps in prioritizing tasks and mitigating the risk of further delays. E. Work with the team to identify options to accelerate project delivery: Collaborating with the team to find ways to accelerate delivery can help make up for lost time. This might include techniques such as crashing, fast-tracking, or redistributing work among available resources. These actions help to directly address the issues causing the delays and involve key stakeholders and the team in finding and implementing solutions.

questions.q: Close to the end of a project, a customer claims that some deliverables have not been met and starts initiating change requests. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Refer to the requirements traceability matrix.
Revise the project scope baseline.
Escalate the change request to the project sponsor.
Review the approved project charter.

questions.e: Refer to the requirements traceability matrix: The requirements traceability matrix (RTM) is a tool that links project requirements to their deliverables. By referring to the RTM, the project manager can verify whether the deliverables in question were part of the original project requirements and scope. This helps in determining if the customer's claims are valid and whether the change requests are justified based on the project's agreed-upon scope and requirements. This approach ensures that the project manager addresses the customer's concerns based on documented evidence, maintaining control over scope and preventing unnecessary changes.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to a long-term project. The project manager came across a government debate over a new law that may affect the project. What are the first two actions the project manager should perform? (Choose two) *

o.t: Create a change request to discuss with the change control board (CCB).
Request additional budget for contingency.
Perform a risk identification process with the project team.
Consult with the project stakeholders.
Discuss the possible impacts with subject matter experts (SMEs).

questions.e: C. Perform a risk identification process with the project team: The first step in addressing potential impacts from the new law is to identify and document the risks. By conducting a risk identification process, the project manager can determine how the new law might affect the project and what specific risks need to be managed. E. Discuss the possible impacts with subject matter experts (SMEs): Consulting with SMEs provides expert insights into how the new law could impact the project. SMEs can help in understanding the potential implications and in developing strategies to mitigate or address these risks. These actions ensure that the project manager is proactive in identifying and assessing the risks associated with the new law, enabling informed decision-making and effective risk management.

questions.q: At the end of a project with multiple suppliers, the project manager is reviewing the closing process and finds that an unexpected financial balance is remaining. What will help the project manager understand why this has occurred? *

o.t: Project audit.
Lessons learned.
Organizational process assets.
Procurement audit.

questions.e: By conducting a procurement audit, the project manager can understand why there is an unexpected financial balance remaining, as it helps in reviewing payments, deliverables, and any contractual terms with suppliers.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project that is in an advanced stage. All high-level risks identified in the risk management plan have been resolved or are no longer a risk for the project. Only low-level risks remain. What should the project manager do now? *

o.t: Reduce the priority of project risks as all remaining risks are low-level.
Notify stakeholders that all high-level risks have been resolved.
Reevaluate identified risks and update the risk register.
Reclassify low-level risks as high-level risks.

questions.e: Reevaluate identified risks and update the risk register: Even though the high-level risks have been resolved or are no longer a concern, it is important to continuously monitor and reassess all risks, including low-level risks. The project environment can change, and new risks might emerge or low-level risks might escalate. By reevaluating and updating the risk register, the project manager ensures that the project remains proactive in risk management throughout its lifecycle. This approach maintains diligent risk management practices, ensuring that all risks are appropriately managed and documented.

questions.q: A project team's performance has declined for the last three iterations. Some of the team members are disappointed, and raise their concerns during the retrospective meeting. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Focus on remediation not merely on correcting symptoms.
Compare the team's performance against other project teams.
Identify potential failure points based on the iteration workload.
Motivate the team to perform better.

questions.e: While identifying potential failure points based on the iteration workload can help in understanding where things might have gone wrong, it is a more reactive approach and may not address the underlying root causes. This option focuses on analyzing the workload and pinpointing where failures occurred, which is helpful, but it does not necessarily lead to long-term solutions or improvements.

questions.q: An agile project is running its second of six iterations. One new team member who does not have agile experience has just joined the team. In the daily meetings, the project manager observes that the team is having problems meeting their goals. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Provide feedback to the team and conduct a meeting to review the team rules.
Provide feedback to the team and conduct a retrospective meeting to find a root cause.
Provide feedback to the team and request agile training for the new member.
Provide feedback to the team and coach the new team member in agile methodology.

questions.e: By conducting a retrospective meeting, the project manager and the team can collaboratively identify the root causes of their struggles, including any challenges posed by the new team member's lack of agile experience. This collective problem-solving approach is a key practice in agile methodologies, helping the team to learn from their experiences and improve their processes and performance continuously.

questions.q: The project is delayed due to the high amount of major changes requested by different stakeholders at different stages of the project. If the project continues on the same path, it will consume twice the time and budget planned. What two actions can the project manager take to be more cost effective? (Choose two) *

o.t: Conduct a stakeholder analysis.
Reinforce team communication.
Update the project management plan with the new timeline.
Adopt an incremental approach.
Leverage work between team members.

questions.e: A. Conduct a stakeholder analysis. Understanding the stakeholders' needs and priorities can help the project manager identify which changes are critical and which can be deferred or managed differently. This can reduce unnecessary changes and align stakeholder expectations, making the project more cost-effective. D. Adopt an incremental approach. An incremental approach allows for delivering parts of the project in stages, making it easier to manage changes and their impacts. This approach can help control costs and timelines by allowing the team to adjust to changes more flexibly and iteratively.

questions.q: For a project has reported the potential for a delivery delay due to a technical issue with the sub-supplier. To stay on schedule, the vendor proposed replacing the sub- supplier's component with a similar part that is different from the one that is stipulated in the project specifications. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Accept the proposed replacement in order to keep procurement activities on track.
Insist on using the component per the project specifications and air freight the equipment to mitigate the delay.
Instruct the vendor to use the part that is compliant with the project specifications and update the schedule.
Consult with a subject matter expert (SME) to see if the proposed change is acceptable.

questions.e: Consulting with a subject matter expert (SME) ensures that the replacement part meets the project's requirements and does not compromise the project's integrity or quality. This step is crucial before making any decision about accepting or rejecting the proposed replacement, as it provides an informed basis for the decision.

questions.q: A team is currently working on a mobile app solution. During sprint execution, one of the developers requires clarification about the acceptance criteria for a particular task. What should the project manager do to obtain the information required by the developer? *

o.t: Request direction from the project sponsor.
Write an email to the client requesting clarification.
Seek support from the development manager.
Work with the product owner to clarify the requirement.

questions.e: In agile projects, the product owner is responsible for defining and clarifying the acceptance criteria and requirements. The project manager should collaborate with the product owner to ensure that the developer has the necessary information to proceed with the task. This maintains alignment with the project's goals and ensures the developer's work meets the client's needs.

questions.q: Important projects in the portfolio backlog need to be delivered. Budget estimates are needed to prioritize the projects. How should the project budgets be estimated? *

o.t: The project is decomposed into features and based on the feature value and the velocity of the team, the team provides the estimate.
Budget estimates are provided based on the experience of the sponsor, product owner and team facilitator.
The team facilitator uses historical data and arrives at an estimate based on the nature of the project.
The product owner obtains all project details and based on the team's experience and velocity provides a budget estimate.

questions.e: Decomposing the project into features and estimating based on feature value and team velocity is a systematic and data-driven approach. It aligns with agile practices, ensuring that estimates are grounded in the team's actual performance and the value delivered by each feature. This method helps create more accurate and realistic budget estimates, which are crucial for project prioritization.

questions.q: In a construction project for a new building, the project manager decides to apply agile principles for the building foundation phase. While evaluating the project schedule with the team, the project manager believes that the estimates are inaccurate. How should the project manager address this issue? *

o.t: Create a product backlog.
Perform sprint reviews with the team.
Assess the previous project velocity.
Reduce the story size by splitting stories.

questions.e: Assessing the previous project velocity helps the project manager understand the team's past performance and use it as a basis for more accurate future estimates. This approach leverages historical data to improve the reliability of the schedule and helps in setting realistic expectations for the project timeline.

questions.q: A software project using an agile approach is facing quality issues with every release, generating many production problems. What should the project manager do to fix the problem and improve the quality? *

o.t: Seek extra funding approval with the sponsor to replace junior team members for more experienced ones.
Create a reward system granting incentives to the team members who are able to catch more defects.
Hire an external company to add an additional layer of testing, making sure that the final product is well inspected before releasing.
Use the retrospective meeting to better understand the root cause of the quality problems and put together a plan with the team to address the problems.

questions.e: Agile practices emphasize continuous improvement, and the retrospective meeting is a key mechanism for identifying and addressing issues. By using the retrospective to understand the root cause of the quality problems, the team can collaboratively develop a plan to improve processes and practices, leading to better quality in future releases.

questions.q: A project manager realizes that the team members are new to the hybrid approach and do not value standup meetings. Team members often arrive late. Digress into solutioning or skip the meetings altogether. How should the project manager improve this situation with the project team? *

o.t: Engage the project team In implementing and Improving key aspects of the standup meetings.
Ask the product owner to remove team members who do not comply with standup meeting rules.
Send a daily retrospective report to all team members instead of holding standup meetings.
Include a daily brainstorming session in the standup meetings to resolve pending.

questions.e: Engaging the team in implementing and improving standup meetings helps to increase their buy-in and ownership of the process. By involving the team in defining how the standups should be conducted and what value they bring, the project manager can foster a sense of responsibility and improve adherence to the meetings, making them more effective and valued by the team.

questions.q: A project manager for a building construction project is planning to go on vacation midway through the project execution phase. What should the project manager do first to ensure the team is empowered and deadlines are met? *

o.t: Allow the team to make decisions to stay on schedule.
Postpone the vacation to a different time.
Ask the project sponsor to make any necessary decisions.
Analyze the impacts and create a plan for team decision making.

questions.e: By analyzing the impacts and creating a plan for team decision-making, the project manager ensures that the team is prepared to handle responsibilities and make decisions in their absence. This proactive approach helps maintain project momentum and ensures that the team is empowered to meet deadlines and address any issues that arise.

questions.q: An agile team is working on a project that will be launched in six countries. Each country has specific requirements in addition to the base offering. The estimates indicate it will take six months to develop the base offering and an additional month to finalize each country’s unique requirements. The expected revenue for the product is the same for each country. Which release strategy should the project manager recommend? *

o.t: A risk-based strategy to maximize the perceived value of the product by launching it to the countries with the lowest technical complexity.
An iterative-based strategy to maximize value by releasing the product to each country as it is finalized and ready for release in that country.
A quality-based strategy to maximize post-market adoption by releasing the product to the countries with the lowest probability of reporting field issues.
A financial-based strategy to reduce the roll-out effort and costs by planning a single, bundled release to all countries at the same time.

questions.e: An iterative-based strategy allows for delivering value incrementally by releasing the product to each country as soon as its unique requirements are finalized. This approach maximizes value by getting the product to market sooner in each country, rather than waiting for all country-specific requirements to be completed. It also enables the team to gather feedback and make improvements progressively.

questions.q: Experienced team members assigned to a critical project are also supporting several other projects and this is delaying the critical project. If this critical project is not delivered, the company could receive a fine from the government. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Discuss the issue with the project sponsor.
Review the resources required for the tasks on the critical path.
Review and update the risk management plan.
Allocate resources to develop the competencies of the other team members.

questions.e: Reviewing the resources required for the tasks on the critical path helps the project manager identify the specific resource bottlenecks causing delays. By addressing these critical path tasks, the project manager can ensure that the most important activities needed to complete the project on time are prioritized, thereby reducing the risk of incurring fines.

questions.q: A project team with members from many different countries is struggling to cooperate. The project manager accepted these difficulties during the storming phase of team development, but the team has not moved to the next phase. The project is beginning to fall behind schedule. What can the project manager do to move the team to the norming phase? *

o.t: Plan social activities to help foster stronger interpersonal relationships and identify shared goals.
Speak with the project sponsor about changing the team composition
Figure out who is behind the issues and apply progressive disciplinary techniques.
Show the team the schedule impact of their communication issues and encourage them to put their differences aside.

questions.e: Social activities can help build stronger interpersonal relationships among team members, promoting trust and understanding. This can facilitate the transition from the storming phase to the norming phase, where the team works more cohesively and efficiently. Identifying shared goals during these activities can also align the team’s efforts towards common objectives, improving cooperation and project performance.

questions.q: A project manager receives a call from the customer's account manager requesting support for a critical operational issue. Although the issue is unrelated to the project, the customer believes that one of the project team members has the technical expertise to recommend a solution. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Organize a conference call with the internal expert and the client to estimate the amount of effort required to fix it.
Decline the request politely since the issue, although critical, is not the responsibility of the project team.
Allocate a task to the team member as a high priority and inform the customer that the issue will be resolved the next day.
Inform the customer that they should contact the sales manager and submit a formal request for a quote.

questions.e: In this case, although the operational issue is critical, it is unrelated to the project and falls outside the project team’s scope. The customer is seeking expertise from a project team member, but this might be better handled outside the project framework. Clarifying the Role: The project team should remain focused on the project. By directing the customer to the sales manager, the project manager is making it clear that this is a separate request, and it should be handled via the proper channels. Business Opportunity: The issue may involve a service or expertise that is outside the project scope but could be turned into a billable opportunity. Referring the customer to the sales manager helps ensure that any support provided is properly formalized and compensated. Professionalism: This response ensures the project manager remains professional, guides the customer toward the correct process, and doesn't compromise the project team's focus.

questions.q: The project manager just started leading a project team from which the previous project manager resigned. After a quick evaluation of the project it is apparent that team morale is low due to continuous disagreement about how to complete tasks. Tasks are taking longer than forecasted and the project is off schedule. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Conduct a meeting with the project team to discuss and address the sources of disagreement.
Inform the stakeholders that the project will be delayed due to previous team management.
Crash the project timeline to ensure the project is back on schedule.
Issue a change request to extend the project schedule based on identified delays.

questions.e: Conducting a meeting with the project team to discuss and address the sources of disagreement is the best approach. It allows the project manager to understand the issues affecting team morale and task completion. By addressing these issues directly, the project manager can facilitate better communication and collaboration within the team, which can lead to improved morale and more accurate task completion.

questions.q: A project manager is starting a project using a hybrid approach and notices some team members only have knowledge of predictive approaches. What does the project manager need to do first in order to have good project performance? *

o.t: Coach those team members lacking hybrid knowledge to learn on the job.
Change the team to include hybrid experts.
Assess the required training per team member.
Deliver hybrid training to all team members.

questions.e: Assessing the required training per team member is the first step in ensuring good project performance. This approach allows the project manager to identify the specific knowledge gaps and provide targeted training, ensuring that all team members have the necessary skills and knowledge to work effectively in a hybrid environment.

questions.q: A newly formed team has become accustomed to agile practices. The project lead has noticed that while they are performing according to expectations, there is boredom with daily team practices among many of the team members. What should the project lead do in this situation? *

o.t: Challenge the team to find new ways to achieve higher levels of performance to improve the situation.
Speak with individual team members to determine what they would like to do to improve the situation in the team.
Have the team inform senior management of the situation and ask for recommendations.
Allow the team to self-organize and have them analyze the situation in their retrospective session and self correct.

questions.e: Allowing the team to self-organize and analyze the situation during their retrospective session aligns with agile principles. It empowers the team to identify and implement improvements themselves, fostering ownership and engagement. This approach helps the team address boredom and find ways to reinvigorate their daily practices.

questions.q: In a project using a hybrid approach, the performance of the team was consistently excellent during the predictive stages. When the iterations began, however, the team members started to show signs of low commitment, conflicts, and confusion, resulting in low morale. What should the project manager do to handle this situation? *

o.t: Give team members more authority to make decisions.
Perform team-building activities and enhance collaboration.
Identify the team members who are impacting low morale.
Coach the team members on agile processes and knowledge.

questions.e: To handle the situation where a team shows signs of low commitment, conflicts, and confusion during the iterations of a hybrid project, the project manager should focus on coaching the team members on agile processes and knowledge. This approach addresses the root causes of the issues by helping the team adapt to the new methodology, reducing confusion, improving collaboration, and enhancing overall commitment.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project which shows a trend to exceed the cost baseline. What should the project manager do first to manage the budget? *

o.t: Ask the project sponsor for assistance in getting the budget back on track.
Meet with the project team to analyze the actual cost to determine deviations.
Inform the stakeholders that the project will be finished over budget.
Issue a change request including the analysis to increase the budget.

questions.e: Meeting with the project team to analyze the actual cost and determine deviations is the first step in managing the budget. This approach allows the project manager to understand the specific reasons for the cost overruns, identify any potential mismanagement or unforeseen expenses, and develop a plan to address these issues. By thoroughly analyzing the cost deviations, the project manager can make informed decisions on how to bring the budget back on track.

questions.q: The project sponsor of a major initiative is consistently changing the prioritization of modular work packages. The team is used to three week sprints and is becoming increasingly frustrated with the daily changes in scope. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Move to a Kanban strategy so that work can be reallocated more easily.
Decrease the sprint cycle to the average reprioritization request by calculating it in days.
Set up a meeting with the project team and ask for their opinion on what to do.
Set up a meeting with the sponsor to explain the importance of keeping a strict sprint cycle.

questions.e: Setting up a meeting with the sponsor to explain the importance of keeping a strict sprint cycle is essential to address the issue of frequent scope changes. The project manager should communicate the negative impact of daily reprioritization on team morale and productivity and highlight how a stable sprint cycle can lead to more predictable and higher-quality outcomes. This approach seeks to align the sponsor's expectations with the agile process, ensuring a more stable work environment for the team.

questions.q: A company is changing their current business model. The change requires implementing a complex project using multiple agile teams. What three options should the project manager have the testing team adopt as testing mechanisms? (Choose three) *

o.t: Independent personal testing
Security and performance testing
An experimental approach to cover all possible choices
Story testing
Tests based on behavior and test-driven development

questions.e: B. Security and performance testing: Ensuring the system is secure and performs well under expected loads is crucial for the success of any complex project. Security and performance testing help identify vulnerabilities and performance bottlenecks. D. Story testing: Story testing involves testing the functionality described in user stories, ensuring that each feature meets the specified requirements and works as intended. This approach aligns well with agile methodologies. E. Tests based on behavior and test-driven development: Behavior-driven development (BDD) and test-driven development (TDD) focus on defining the behavior of the system through tests before the actual development begins. This ensures that the code meets the specified behavior and requirements from the outset, leading to higher quality and more reliable software.

questions.q: A globally distributed project team is running behind schedule due to the lack of team commitment and low morale. In order to bring the schedule back on track, what should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Seek the sponsor's approval to extend the project schedule.
Set up a meeting to perform a root cause analysis.
Update the issue log and communicate it to the team.
Permanently colocate the team for better performance.

questions.e: Setting up a meeting to perform a root cause analysis is the first step in addressing the issue. This approach helps to identify the underlying causes of the lack of commitment and low morale, allowing the project manager to develop targeted solutions to improve team performance and bring the project schedule back on track. Understanding the root causes is crucial before taking any further actions, such as seeking schedule extensions or relocating the team.

questions.q: A key team member shared confidential information about another team member with management, a practice that is against ethical standards. During a team meeting, some of the team members requested that the key team member be removed from the team. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Contact the human resource (HR) department for a solution.
Speak with the key team member to clarify the situation.
Conduct a meeting with the team to deliberate on a decision.
Suspend the team member until further notice.

questions.e: Speaking with the key team member to clarify the situation is the appropriate next step. This allows the project manager to understand the context and details of the incident directly from the involved party. It is important to gather all relevant information before making any decisions or taking further action. This approach also ensures fair treatment and gives the key team member an opportunity to explain their actions.

questions.q: During project execution, a key team member has to be moved to another critical project for the company. Currently, there is no other team member who can fill that role. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Communicate the problem to the sponsor to force the key member to be maintained on the project.
Initiate a change request and replace the key member as soon as possible.
Explain to the company the importance of maintaining the key member on the project according to the vision of the project.
Evaluate the impact of the key team member's removal from the project, look for alternatives, and submit a change request if required.

questions.e: Evaluating the impact of the key team member's removal from the project allows the project manager to understand the potential consequences and explore possible alternatives. This approach ensures that the decision is made based on a thorough analysis of the situation. If necessary, the project manager can then submit a change request with a well-founded justification for any proposed adjustments to the project plan.

questions.q: An experienced project manager is managing a multi-million dollar agile project. The project manager communicates the ground rules to the team but after 12 iterations, the project manager starts noticing that some team members are not following the ground rules. What should the project manager do first to ensure team adherence to the ground rules? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with the project team to reinforce the ground rules.
Notify the project sponsor about this behavior and ask the sponsor to take disciplinary action.
Contact human resources to request a written warning letter be sent to team members not following the ground rules.
Ask the functional manager to replace team members not following the ground rules.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting with the project team to reinforce the ground rules is the best first step. It allows the project manager to address the issue directly with the team, remind them of the importance of the ground rules, and discuss any challenges or misunderstandings that might be causing the non-adherence. This approach promotes open communication and provides an opportunity to reset expectations without immediately escalating the issue.

questions.q: A company is helping their client launch an Innovative product. During the sprint review, the product owner identifies that the product does not include key features that were previously prioritized as part of the product backlog. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Extend the sprint timeline so the learn can work on the missing feature.
Inform the product owner that this issue needs to be escalated to the executive level.
Collaborate with the product owner and the team to plan the following sprint
Initiate the change request process to include these missing features.

questions.e: Collaborating with the product owner and the team to plan the following sprint is the appropriate next step. This approach ensures that the missing features are reprioritized and included in the upcoming sprint backlog. It allows for an agile response to the feedback received during the sprint review, maintaining the iterative nature of agile development and focusing on continuous improvement.

questions.q: The business manager and the product owner are requesting a more flexible way to incorporate changes into the product baseline. They are concerned about losing time to market with respect to other vendors. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the assumption log and project management plan for changes.
Identify adequate change management tools to conduct the project.
Establish a change control board (CCB) with key stakeholders.
Allow key stakeholders to make some changes to deliver the product faster.

questions.e: Identifying and implementing appropriate change management tools can help the team quickly incorporate changes into the product baseline without formal and potentially slow approval processes.

questions.q: According to the project contract the delivery date is approaching. However one important material is still not on site. The construction work will have to stop and wait for this special material, delaying the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Record it in the risk register.
Ask the client to help solve the problem.
Start procuring this material from another supplier.
Engage the project team to look for alternatives to find a solution.

questions.e: Engaging the project team to look for alternatives to find a solution is the best course of action. This approach leverages the collective expertise and creativity of the team to identify potential solutions that could mitigate the delay. Alternatives might include finding a different supplier, expediting the current order, or finding a temporary workaround to keep the project moving.

questions.q: A project is nearing completion. The contingency time has been consumed. To ensure that the final deliverables are achieved in budget, the project manager has asked the team to follow a rigorous process. This i s causing some resistance among the team members. What should the project manager do to address the growing resistance? *

o.t: Crash the project schedule and ask project team members to work overtime to meet the new timeline.
Motivate project team members by offering incentives to complete the project on time.
Describe to the team members how specific tools and techniques can be used to finish on time.
Convince team members to use a specific methodology to complete the project on time.

questions.e: This approach educates the team on the benefits and practical applications of the process, potentially reducing resistance by showing how it can help achieve the project goals effectively. It also fosters a collaborative environment where team members feel more engaged and informed.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a major construction project. Part of the agreed-upon plan was to use a cloud-based system with a server that runs on high-speed internet service since most of the team members work virtually. The company needs to reduce operating costs as much as possible and management insists that the project will now use a system running on a conventional dial-up service. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Evaluate the impact of this decision and communicate with management.
Agree with management and continue working the project management plan.
Meet with management about their decision and ask them to get another project manager.
Replace some of the team members that work virtually to help the company save money.

questions.e: Evaluating the impact of the decision and communicating with management ensures that the project manager thoroughly understands the potential consequences of switching to a dial-up service. This includes assessing how it will affect project timelines, team productivity, and overall project success. By presenting this analysis to management, the project manager can provide a data-driven perspective to help reconsider the decision or find alternative solutions that balance cost reduction with project needs.

questions.q: A project just kicked off and management’s expectation is to ensure that the deliverable of the first iteration helps the marketing team present the product prototype to potential customers. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Increase the details of the work breakdown structure (WBS) to minimize errors and delays.
Split the backlog into phases to ensure that the key features are delivered first.
Ask the sponsor to prioritize some functionalities of the product.
Identify the minimum functionality required for the product.

questions.e: Identifying the minimum functionality required for the product ensures that the first iteration delivers a prototype with the essential features needed for the marketing team to present to potential customers. This approach focuses on the core elements that demonstrate the product's value, making it easier to create a functional and compelling prototype within the given timeframe.

questions.q: During the course of a project the project manager's immediate director is communicating directly with the client to approve changes without the project manager's knowledge. This is causing confusion in the project team where the scope is changing in the background, but only being mentioned in project meetings. How should the project manager handle this? *

o.t: Communicate directly with the director and inform them of the communications management plan.
Communicate directly with the client stating that any scope changes must go through the project manager.
Review the stakeholder engagement plan and put in place any existing actions accordingly.
Discuss the issues with the project team and let them know that the project manager will handle scope changes.

questions.e: Communicating directly with the director and informing them of the communications management plan ensures that all changes follow the established process, reducing confusion and maintaining control over the project scope. This approach helps clarify roles and responsibilities, ensuring that all stakeholders are aligned with the project's communication protocols.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project which has a very complex and long execution period Although the project is mostly predictive, the team was able to break the design and execution into smaller packages using a hybrid framework. The business wants to keep track of the value delivered by this framework application but there is no defined set of measurable items for the framework. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Work with the stakeholders to determine which measurable benefits can be tracked and assign an accountable person to monitor and report them.
Create a report based on the work breakdown structure (WBS) and update it on a regular basis.
Use the same benefits tracking process from the last predictive project and add this to the monthly status report.
Research which templates of reports were used the most for this framework and incorporate them into the project.

questions.e: Collaborating with stakeholders to determine which measurable benefits can be tracked ensures that the project aligns with the business's goals and provides value. Assigning an accountable person to monitor and report these benefits helps maintain focus and provides clear accountability, enabling the project to demonstrate its progress and value effectively.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to an important company project. While reviewing the lessons learned from a similar, previous project, the project manager finds that the biggest challenges were related to learn motivation. What should the project manager do to avoid these challenges? *

o.t: Increase the project budget by 10% for team-related activities and awards.
Plan to implement team-building strategies throughout the project.
Ask the functional manager to motivate the team outside of the project.
Colocate the team to encourage more motivational team activities.

questions.e: Implementing team-building strategies throughout the project helps to continuously foster motivation, collaboration, and a positive team environment. This proactive approach addresses potential motivation challenges by keeping the team engaged and cohesive, leading to better project performance and overall success.

questions.q: The project manager has learned that the project sponsor is unhappy with the development of the project requirements. In order to realign the project with the sponsor's expectations. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the project goal diagram with the team.
Perform a stakeholder evaluation.
Confirm which templates the team should be using.
Review the risk management plan.

questions.e: By reviewing the project goal diagram with the team, the project manager can ensure that the project’s objectives are clearly understood and aligned with the sponsor’s expectations. This step helps in identifying any discrepancies between the project’s goals and the sponsor’s requirements, allowing for adjustments to be made to realign the project with the sponsor's expectations.

questions.q: A project manager is working to create a product that can be released to the market as soon as it passes rigorous quality standards. Historically, the company has used a predictive methodology, but the company is exploring the implementation of agile methodologies. The company asked the project manager to explain the value gained by using an agile process. How should the project manager respond? *

o.t: Early value cannot be achieved until the product is fully released.
Early value can be gained by testing the most important features in the initial stages to fix deviations.
Early value will be gained only if beta products can be released to the market.
Early value will be gained only if the speed can be increased to release the product to the market.

questions.e: Using an agile process allows the team to focus on developing and testing the most important features early in the project. This enables the identification and fixing of deviations and issues in the initial stages, providing early value and allowing for iterative improvements. This approach helps ensure that the product meets quality standards and stakeholder expectations more effectively.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a software development project. A team member complains that since the project tasks are very simple, there is no reason to perform quality control. The project manager understands that removing the quality management plan from the project will also help to save money, which is important to the customer. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Register starting the project without a quality management plan as a risk, and allocate the budget savings to the management reserve.
Develop the quality management plan, as quality is as equally important as cost and schedule management.
Get confirmation from management that the team member has enough experience to build software without quality control.
Ask the customer to order an external quality audit after accepting the project deliverable, and decrease the budget of the project.

questions.e: Quality management is crucial to ensuring that the project deliverables meet the required standards and satisfy the customer. Developing a quality management plan helps to identify and address potential issues early, preventing costly rework and ensuring the project meets its objectives. Ignoring quality control can lead to defects and failures that may ultimately increase costs and harm customer satisfaction.

questions.q: The project charter was just approved and the project sponsor has given permission to proceed with the project. The program manager has confirmed that one of the requested key resources is also needed on another project at the same time. This will affect project delivery What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Pay overtime to key resource to get the work done outside of working hours.
Have a meeting with project manager of the other project to find a resource optimization solution that works for both projects.
Speak with the client to see if the project delivery deadline can be delayed due to resource availability.
Talk to the program manager and about prioritizing this project over other projects so the key resources are available.

questions.e: Collaborating with the project manager of the other project to find a resource optimization solution allows both projects to address the resource conflict in a mutually beneficial way. This approach helps ensure that both projects can proceed without significant delays or additional costs and promotes effective use of shared resources.

questions.q: A large company has agreed on a business case for an environmental project. The project will cause some major changes in their operations, such as reduction in paper use, which will obviously affect all of the users. What is the first thing the appointed project manager should do? *

o.t: Evaluate the impact to the users and create a plan to address it.
Inform users about the new changes and ask for their collaboration.
Ask all managers to collaborate implementing this change to users.
Start implementing the change so that users will eventually get used to it.

questions.e: Evaluating the impact to the users and creating a plan to address it ensures that the project manager understands how the changes will affect the users and can develop strategies to manage these impacts effectively.

questions.q: The project sponsor recently requested that a vendor begins working toward adopting a hybrid approach. In response, the vendor hired a project manager experienced in agile for the project. What does that project manager need to do to make the team work in a collaborative way? *

o.t: Request the project management office (PMO) for a team of mentors.
Allocate time to mentor the team.
Update the issue log.
Identify any training gaps.

questions.e: Allocating time to mentor the team ensures that the team members understand agile principles and practices and can effectively collaborate in the new hybrid approach. Mentoring helps build the necessary skills and fosters a collaborative culture, which is crucial for the successful adoption of agile methodologies within the hybrid framework.

questions.q: A few developers have submitted their resignation after completing their annual review and receiving their annual bonus. The project manager cannot find replacements for all of the developers in time to meet the project's deadline. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Request additional budget to recruit more developers.
Lower the recruitment criteria.
Log the issue in the issue log.
Analyze the impact and inform the stakeholders.

questions.e: Analyzing the impact and informing the stakeholders ensures that all parties are aware of the potential consequences of the resignations on the project timeline and deliverables. This approach allows for a collaborative effort to find solutions, such as adjusting the project schedule, reallocating resources, or finding other ways to mitigate the impact.

questions.q: A project manager has a team of shared resources from other projects who are working on a client project . Three days before the project is due, t he team informs the project manager that the project will be delayed because a component was not delivered on time. Competing priorities of the shared resources are delaying delivery of the component. What should the project manager have done to prevent this delay from happening? *

o.t: Updated the risk management plan and registered lessons learned for the project.
Reorganized the team for the project based on the work breakdown structure (WBS).
Maintained constant communication with the stakeholders of the other projects.
Used the resource management plan to identify the impacts of the other projects.

questions.e: Using the resource management plan to identify the impacts of other projects would have allowed the project manager to anticipate and mitigate conflicts arising from shared resources. This plan helps in understanding the allocation and availability of resources, enabling better scheduling and prioritization to prevent delays due to competing priorities.

questions.q: A company recently used desktop research for a feasibility study, which showed that the project is behind schedule. The project team also has concerns about the impact of scope changes on the project schedule. What should the project manager do to keep the project on schedule while still meeting project objectives? *

o.t: Collaborate with the change control board (CCB) to review the scope and submit any change requests.
Submit a change request to the CCB and update the schedule.
Update the scope and add more resources to the project.
Update the scope and move on to the next project milestone.

questions.e: Collaborating with the change control board (CCB) to review the scope and submit any change requests ensures that changes are properly evaluated and approved through a formal process. This helps maintain control over the project scope and schedule, ensuring that any adjustments are aligned with the project objectives and stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: During the closing process, the project manager learns that one deliverable is not meeting customer expectations. How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Ask the customer to issue a change request with the information to analyze and provide a solution.
Review the deliverable requirements, check the customer approval criteria, and proceed accordingly.
Meet with the customer to reach agreement on the scope of the deliverable that will satisfy both parties.
Contact the project sponsor and ask for help in negotiating the closing of the project with the customer.

questions.e: Reviewing the deliverable requirements and checking the customer approval criteria ensures that the project manager understands the basis for the customer's expectations and whether the deliverable meets the agreed-upon standards. This step allows the project manager to determine if there is a legitimate issue with the deliverable or if the expectations were beyond the agreed scope. Based on this review, the project manager can take appropriate action to address the situation.

questions.q: In a functional organization, a product analyst is assigned to a short-duration application development effort. The analyst expresses concerns about the task and asks the project manager to provide the support of a peer with expertise in this domain. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Make sure the analyst has regular pairing meetings with the other team member throughout task execution.
Ask the analyst to use skills to develop the tool, then move development to another team member.
Enroll the analyst in a capacity-building program and keep this analyst assigned to the task.
Recognize the analyst's concerns and reassign the task to another team member.

questions.e: In a functional organization, resources may be limited, and reassigning tasks might not always be feasible. Pairing the analyst with a peer who has expertise in the domain allows for knowledge sharing and skill development while still progressing with the task. This approach addresses the analyst's concerns by providing the needed support and ensures that the project continues without delays. Regular pairing meetings facilitate collaboration and help the analyst build confidence and expertise in the domain.

questions.q: A project manager finds that team members in an agile project are involved in several different projects due to budget constraints. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Request the project sponsor prioritize and if necessary, allocate additional budget so the team can work on a single project.
Provide an incentive plan so the team members will work more unaccounted hours on multiple projects.
Brainstorm with the team members on how they can deliver on multiple projects within the given budget.
Instruct the team members to spread evenly across projects so mistakes will not occur within the current budget.

questions.e: This approach leverages the team's collective knowledge and experience, encourages ownership, and can lead to innovative ways to optimize efficiency and productivity without requiring additional resources. It fosters a supportive environment where team members can contribute ideas and agree on strategies that work best for them, ensuring better engagement and commitment to project success.

questions.q: A project manager has received a new request to integrate more features to a product. The team is fully allocated, and there is no budget to acquire new resources. What strategy should the project manager implement to deal with this situation? *

o.t: Ask the team to accelerate the iterations and avoid interruptions.
Discuss the problem with the team and decide how to do the work together.
Verify team performance and ask for improvement during daily standup meetings.
Recommend that the project sponsor increases the budget to bring new resources.

questions.e: Involving the team in discussions about how to handle new requests is a core agile practice. The team can collectively assess the impact of the additional features, prioritize the work, and determine how best to integrate the new requirements without overburdening themselves. This approach ensures transparency, fosters collaboration, and leverages the team's insights to find a feasible solution within the existing constraints.

questions.q: The customer's project manager changes during the final stage of a project. How can the project manager avoid a project closure delay? *

o.t: Update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Review the latest project status report and update the stakeholders.
Escalate the case to the customer's management team.
Issue the project payment invoice to the customer in advance.

questions.e: When there is a change in a key stakeholder, such as the customer's project manager, updating the stakeholder engagement plan is crucial. This plan outlines how to communicate and engage with stakeholders throughout the project. By updating it, the project manager can ensure that the new project manager is properly informed, aligned with the project's status, and understands the closure process. This proactive step helps in avoiding delays and ensures a smooth transition and project closure.

questions.q: After reviewing the project management plan with key stakeholders, the project manager was told that an 18-month release plan was unacceptable and the product should launch in six months. Based on the new timeline, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Plan for overtime apply crashing and fast tracking and share the risk of failure with project stakeholders.
Review the project backlog looking for high-priority items and come up with a minimum viable product (MVP) that fits the expected timeline.
Seek approval with the sponsor to triple the project budget, hiring more people to compensate for the compressed schedule.
Go over the critical path with stakeholders, explaining why it is not possible to deliver all the scope in the expected timeline.

questions.e: When stakeholders mandate a significantly shorter timeline, it is often impractical to deliver the full scope of the project within the new constraints. The best approach is to identify the high-priority items that deliver the most value and create a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). This ensures that the product can be launched within the required timeframe while still delivering essential functionality. This approach aligns with agile principles and allows for subsequent iterations to enhance the product post-launch.

questions.q: A project manager and a stakeholder have different opinions on the budget estimates for a project that is being initiated based on a new consumer privacy law. What would be a reason for this difference in opinion? *

o.t: The communications management plan was not used by all stakeholders.
Organizational assets were not available to back the rationale.
Relative estimation by the team resulted in two estimates.
The use of the Monte Carlo method can result in different estimations.

questions.e: When there are differing opinions on budget estimates, one common reason is the lack of access to organizational process assets that could provide historical data or guidelines to support the rationale behind the estimates. Organizational assets include documentation from past projects, lessons learned, and historical data, which can help in making more accurate and agreed-upon budget estimates. Without these, stakeholders may base their estimates on differing assumptions or incomplete information, leading to conflicting opinions.

questions.q: A marketing team is planning for a multiyear initiative that will include a lot of cross-functional stakeholders. The project manager has been assigned and is now in the project planning phase. Which item should the project manager develop first? *

o.t: A product backlog and identification of the features to be delivered.
A business case and scope document.
A communications management plan that addresses the team's needs.
A risk management plan to incorporate known risks.

questions.e: During the planning phase, establishing a communications management plan is crucial for ensuring all cross-functional stakeholders are aligned and informed. This plan will facilitate effective communication throughout the project's life cycle, which is especially important for a project with many stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager works for a large manufacturing company with diversified domains. The project team often participates in change requests. Recently, the change control board (CCB) deferred some requests and the project manager wants to communicate these requests to the stakeholders. What document should the project manager use to communicate these requests? *

o.t: Risk log
Change log
Backlog
Issue log

questions.e: The change log is the document used to record and track all change requests, including their status (approved, deferred, or rejected). It serves as a central repository for all change-related information and is essential for communicating the status of change requests to stakeholders. Change Log: This document tracks all change requests, their impact, their status, and any actions taken. It provides stakeholders with a clear view of how changes are being managed and ensures transparency in the change control process.

questions.q: A company wants to increase the commercial value of one of its products in a highly competitive market. In order to do this, the company commissions a project to create a prototype. The team constructs the prototype incrementally. Which action should the project manager take as a priority? *

o.t: Emphasize the use of Kanban methodology.
Ensure the project sponsor is aware of the go-to market date.
Deliver business value as soon as possible.
Implement a plan-do-check-act (PDCA) cycle.

questions.e: In a highly competitive market, the priority for a project aimed at increasing the commercial value of a product should be to deliver business value as soon as possible. This means focusing on creating and delivering a functional prototype quickly to capture market interest, receive early feedback, and make necessary adjustments to enhance the product's commercial value. Delivering business value quickly: Ensures that the project meets its goal of enhancing the product's commercial value and competitiveness. It allows the company to respond to market needs and opportunities promptly.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a new project. Many of the project deliverables need to be outsourced. What should the project manager use to document the project deliverables? *

o.t: Service level agreement (SLA)
Statement of work (SOW)
Scope management plan
Memorandum of understanding (MOU)

questions.e: Statement of Work (SOW): The SOW is a detailed document that outlines the project deliverables, tasks, timelines, and expectations for work that needs to be outsourced. It serves as a formal agreement between the project manager and the vendor, ensuring both parties understand the scope and requirements of the outsourced work. Service Level Agreement (SLA): SLAs are used to define the level of service expected from a vendor, focusing on performance metrics, service quality, and responsibilities, rather than detailing specific deliverables. Scope Management Plan: This plan outlines how the project scope will be defined, validated, and controlled. It does not provide the detailed descriptions of project deliverables needed for outsourcing. Memorandum of Understanding (MOU): MOUs are typically used for mutual agreements between parties, but they are not as detailed or legally binding as a SOW for documenting specific deliverables and requirements.

questions.q: Due to a recent budget reduction, two team members were released from an agile team. The customer is still expecting early results for the project. Which two actions should the project manager take to align customer expectations? (Choose two) *

o.t: Ask the agile team to review the updated sprint velocity with the customer.
Ask the product owner to review the prioritized backlog with the customer.
Ask the agile team to review and update the quality management plan with the customer.
Review the impediments log with the customer.
Send a detailed project management plan to the customer.

questions.e: A. Review the updated sprint velocity: Given the reduction in team members, the team's capacity to complete work within each sprint will be impacted. Reviewing the updated sprint velocity with the customer provides a clear picture of the new pace at which the team can deliver work. This helps set realistic expectations regarding project timelines. B. Review the prioritized backlog: The product owner should review the prioritized backlog with the customer to ensure that the most critical and high-value features are addressed first. This helps in aligning the project's focus with the customer's most urgent needs, making the best use of the available resources.

questions.q: A team has been working together for several months and has successfully delivered work. A new team member has joined the team but is having difficulty contributing. What should the project manager do to help the new team member integrate effectively? *

o.t: Give the new team member time to contribute until they ask for help and support.
Assign the new team member tasks so that the team member knows on what to focus.
Approach the team member to identify any issues and then plan a resolution accordingly.
Review the project with the team member to ensure the project scope is understood.

questions.e: Approaching the new team member to identify any issues they may be facing and then planning a resolution accordingly is the best approach. This allows the project manager to understand the specific challenges the new member is experiencing and to provide targeted support. It fosters open communication and helps integrate the new team member effectively into the existing team.

questions.q: An external project manager is managing the construction of new corporate offices for a large company. The project management plan states that it is necessary to contract a highly trained external resource to revise and validate an important project component. The client has rejected hiring the external resource because of the high cost even though it is within the project budget. What should the project manager do to resolve this issue? *

o.t: Hire the resource in order to achieve the project objectives.
Ask the client for a meeting and explain that the task will not be performed.
Evaluate the consequences and meet with the client to explain the possible scenarios.
Try to accomplish the task internally by leveling resources from other projects.

questions.e: The project manager should evaluate the potential consequences of not hiring the highly trained external resource and present these scenarios to the client. This involves assessing the risks and impacts on the project objectives, quality, and timelines. By providing a thorough analysis, the project manager can help the client understand the importance of hiring the external resource and the potential negative outcomes of not doing so. This approach fosters informed decision-making and ensures that the client is aware of all possible consequences.

questions.q: A team member misses a project meeting without it being approved and has been penalized as defined in the ground rules. This team member, as well as other team members, insist that it is the first time they have seen this rule regarding the project and they do not agree with the penalty. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Ensured the team charter was developed by the team members.
Ensured the team members are fully supportive of all decisions.
Distributed the project charter to all team members.
Used a charismatic leadership style.

questions.e: The team charter should be developed collaboratively by the team members to ensure that everyone is aware of and agrees with the ground rules, roles, responsibilities, and penalties. When team members participate in creating the team charter, they are more likely to understand and support the rules and procedures.
