This collaborative process helps avoid misunderstandings and ensures that all team members are on the same page regarding expectations and consequences.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project that will handle sensitive data for millions of users. The sponsor mentioned that, to their knowledge, the project does not seem to have any compliance requirements in their country. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Request expert advice from the compliance leader to confirm if there are any compliance requirements for the project.
Check with the national compliance agency to determine if the project has any compliance requirements in this country.
Trust in the expertise of the sponsor and believe that there are no compliance requirements for this project.
Conduct independent research regarding the data protection policy of the country for legal.

questions.e: Handling sensitive data for millions of users typically involves compliance with data protection and privacy regulations. Even if the sponsor believes there are no compliance requirements, it is crucial to confirm this with a compliance expert. By requesting expert advice, the project manager ensures that all potential legal and regulatory obligations are identified and addressed, thereby mitigating risks associated with non-compliance.

questions.q: L ocal company is developing a new product and for the first time, using a remote team for the programming tasks of features. The design for the product comes from the local team. During the third sprint review, the product owner has concerns about the project's outcomes. The remote development team is complaining that they do not clearly understand the requirements conveyed in the daily standup meetings. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Evaluate and reassign the developing tasks to a local vendor who has worked on previous projects.
Document the risk in the risk management plan and use contingency reserves to hire a local vendor.
Review lessons learned from previous projects and organizational process assets (OPAs).
Determine the communication needs, environment, and tools to get the message across.

questions.e: In a situation where the remote development team does not clearly understand the requirements, it is crucial to improve communication methods and tools to ensure that everyone is on the same page. By determining the communication needs, environment, and tools, the project manager can facilitate clearer and more effective communication, helping to address the concerns of the product owner and the remote team.

questions.q: An agile team has completed an iteration and delivered the agreed features to the customer. In a surprise to the team, the features are not accepted by the customer. The project team conducts a root cause analysis. What should the project manager do to avoid this situation in the future? *

o.t: Ensure that customer requirements do not change from the start of the project.
Ensure that the definition of done (DoD) is well defined and complete for future iterations.
Ensure that the development and quality assurance team members implement the feature correctly.
Ensure that the team facilitator allocates tasks correctly to team members.

questions.e: The definition of done (DoD) is a key concept in agile methodologies that clearly specifies the criteria that must be met for a feature or user story to be considered complete. Ensuring that the DoD is well defined and complete helps the team to understand the customer's expectations and deliver features that meet those expectations. This reduces the likelihood of surprises and rejections from the customer in the future.

questions.q: A research and development team is finishing up a two year initiative. The project manager is focused on the closing activities for the project. Which activity should be considered as a priority? *

o.t: Mark the product backlog completion status and update the communications management plan.
Ensure that knowledge transfer activities are executed as planned.
Release the resources and plan for a project completion celebration.
Hold a steering committee meeting to inform them of the project completion.

questions.e: Ensuring that knowledge transfer activities are executed as planned is a crucial step during the project closing phase. It helps in retaining valuable information, lessons learned, and best practices that can be used for future projects. This activity ensures that the knowledge gained during the project is not lost and can benefit the organization and other team members.

questions.q: A new team member has joined an agile project, replacing a team member who recently left. The project team needs the new team member to speed up their ability to contribute effectively to the project. What should the project manager do to help in this situation? *

o.t: Assign the new team member the same tasks that were assigned to the previous team member who they replaced.
Schedule knowledge transfer sessions and assign less complex tasks to the new team member.
Send technical documentation to the new team member and schedule training for the next iteration.
Have the new team member complete all of the company’s mandatory training.

questions.e: Scheduling knowledge transfer sessions ensures that the new team member gets the necessary information and context to understand the project quickly. Assigning less complex tasks helps the new team member start contributing effectively without overwhelming them. This approach facilitates a smoother onboarding process and allows the new team member to gradually ramp up their contributions.

questions.q: The project sponsor on an agile project informed the project lead that an executive would like an update on the project’s progress. What should the project lead do? *

o.t: Provide a link to the project's shared drive for the executive to search through for any artifacts that are of interest.
Invite the executive to the project's meeting space to determine if the project information radiators meet their needs.
Reach out to the project management office (PMO) for status report templates and provide project updates in that format.
Ask the project sponsor or product owner to provide an update since the project lead should be trying to keep the team free from impediments.

questions.e: Inviting the executive to the project's meeting space allows them to see the information radiators (such as Kanban boards, burn-down charts, and other visual progress tools) firsthand. This approach aligns with agile principles of transparency and continuous communication. It also ensures that the executive receives accurate and up-to-date information in a format that is already being used by the team.

questions.q: In a weak matrix environment, two key team members are falling behind with their tasks, which will affect the success of the project. Further investigation by the project manager reveals that they have unresolved issues with each other. The project manager asks them to find a way to resolve the issues, but this is unsuccessful. The project manager then holds a meeting with them to work out a permanent solution to the issues, but this is also unsuccessful. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to a higher authority.
Suspend the two key team members immediately.
Put the issue on the agenda for the next team meeting.
Reassign one of the key team members to a different task.

questions.e: The higher authority can intervene to resolve the conflict effectively, ensuring both team members can continue contributing to the project's success.

questions.q: During the implementation phase of a construction project the customer asked a key subcontractor to deliver a work package ahead of time. The subcontractor was not prepared for it and asked the project manager for additional budget. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Ask upper management for more funds and update the project budget.
Revise the project scope accordingly to cope with the budget changes.
Update the risk register and project log and manage the budget closely.
Submit a change request to accelerate the project as requested.

questions.e: When a customer requests an acceleration of a work package that requires additional budget, the appropriate step is to submit a change request. This request should outline the need for additional funds and any other impacts on the project, such as changes to scope or schedule. The change control process will then be followed to review and approve or reject the request. This approach ensures that the project manager formally addresses the customer's request and that any changes are documented and approved through the proper channels.

questions.q: A company is initiating a project to decommission inefficient sales channels. Several stakeholders argue that one channel that indicates a downturn in generating value is still more efficient than some of the channels that are planned to remain. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Plan for incremental and iterative delivery based on feedback from the marketing and sales team.
Review and update the success criteria to ensure that the channel is not decommissioned.
Inform the stakeholders that the list of channels to be decommissioned was approved by the CEO.
Escalate the objection to the steering committee and human resources (HR) as a personal intimidation incident.

questions.e: Planning for incremental and iterative delivery allows the project manager to incorporate feedback from the marketing and sales team, which helps ensure that decisions are based on current and accurate data. This approach enables continuous assessment and adjustment of the project plan, ensuring that only the least efficient channels are decommissioned. This method is responsive to stakeholder concerns and supports data-driven decision-making.

questions.q: In a project management team meeting, one of the team members always argues with the project manager about the objective, timeline, and deliverable of any assigned task. What should the project manager do to manage this conflict? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with the team member and their manager to discuss the issue.
Talk to the project sponsor about the team member's attitude.
Schedule a one-on-one meeting with the team member to talk about it and get their cooperation.
Find another person to replace this team member.

questions.e: By scheduling a one-on-one meeting, the project manager can address the issue privately, understand the team member's concerns, and work towards a resolution. This approach fosters open communication and collaboration, aiming to resolve the conflict constructively and ensure the team member's cooperation. It also demonstrates the project manager's commitment to understanding and resolving team issues, which can help build trust and improve team dynamics.

questions.q: A project manager presented the project schedule to the stakeholders . They have requested that the project be completed two months earlier than the scheduled date. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Hold a stakeholder meeting to align timelines and scope expectations.
Crash the schedule to shorten the timeline while keeping the scope unchanged.
Update the cost management plan to allocate more resources to the project to finish the scope earlier.
Reduce the scope of the project by removing activities and shortening the timeline.

questions.e: When stakeholders request a significant change in the project schedule, such as completing the project two months earlier, it is crucial to first hold a meeting to align timelines and scope expectations. This allows the project manager to understand the stakeholders' reasons for the request, discuss the potential impacts on scope, cost, and quality, and explore feasible options. By aligning expectations, the project manager can ensure that any changes to the schedule are realistic, agreed upon by all parties, and documented appropriately.

questions.q: The sponsor is supportive in leveraging agile approaches. The project manager is contemplating how to roll out the agile approach and gain buy-in from both project team members and stakeholders What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Determine which agile software tools will be required to support agile delivery within the organization.
Select a current predictive project define the approach, and provide agile training to execute the remainder of the project.
Start with a pilot project of appropriate complexity and provide agile training to those who are impacted.
Determine how to transform the organization using agile techniques, including organizational training and communications.

questions.e: Starting with a pilot project allows the organization to gradually adopt agile methodologies on a smaller scale, which can help in identifying potential challenges and benefits before a full-scale rollout. Providing agile training to those impacted ensures that the team and stakeholders understand the principles and practices of agile, which can help gain buy-in and support. This approach allows for learning and adaptation in a controlled environment, making it easier to address issues and refine processes before implementing agile across the entire organization.

questions.q: A project manager created a contingency plan associated with a risk. The risk was realized, but the client insists on using a new workaround instead. The requested workaround will introduce delays and require additional budget. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Request to use the management reserve to keep the schedule.
Mitigate risks associated with the workaround to avoid project delays.
Proceed with the approved risk response plan.
Discuss the options with the client as part of the change control process.

questions.e: The project manager needs to handle the situation in a structured way by engaging the client and discussing the potential impacts of the new workaround. Since the workaround could introduce delays and require additional budget, it is necessary to follow the change control process to evaluate, approve, and document any changes to the project scope, schedule, or budget. The change control process ensures that all stakeholders are aligned and that any potential changes are properly assessed, including the associated costs, risks, and impacts on the project.

questions.q: During the implementation phase of a project, a new regulation affects the project, and a critical status meeting discussing the scope changes is required. The project manager discovers that a key stakeholder cannot attend the scheduled meeting. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Call for a change control board (CCB) meeting, and inform the stakeholder about the outcome.
Update the communications management plan and implement the change.
Meet with the project sponsor to discuss how to address the situation.
Meet with the stakeholder prior to the meeting to obtain their opinion.

questions.e: When a key stakeholder cannot attend a critical status meeting discussing important scope changes due to new regulations, it is essential to obtain their input beforehand. Meeting with the stakeholder prior to the scheduled meeting allows the project manager to understand their perspective, concerns, and recommendations. This ensures that the stakeholder's input is considered during the meeting and helps maintain their engagement and support for the project decisions.

questions.q: A new project manager is assigned to a project in the execution stage. A few key stakeholders inform the new project manager that the project has some serious issues. What should the newly assigned project manager do first to understand the issues? *

o.t: Escalate the issues to the project sponsor.
Review the issues log to ensure the issues are captured.
Check the risk management plan to ensure there is a strategy to address the issues.
Ask the key stakeholders to discuss the issues with the project team.

questions.e: When a new project manager is assigned and informed about serious issues by key stakeholders, the first step should be to review the issues log. This log will provide a comprehensive record of all identified issues, their status, and any actions taken to address them. By reviewing the issues log, the project manager can gain a clear understanding of the issues at hand, assess their impact, and determine the next steps for resolution. This approach ensures that the project manager is well-informed before taking any further actions or making decisions.

questions.q: A project manager is using a hybrid approach for project delivery. The development team was sized, but is not yet fully resourced. The project manager is working on defining the project schedule. What should the project manager do to address the issue of developer availability? *

o.t: Organize a planning session with the development team and use their estimations to complete the schedule.
Ask the resource manager when the new contractor is available to start and change the delivery date for the project schedule.
Ask the sponsor to provide the desired completion date for project activities and complete the schedule.
Use expert judgment to estimate all of the tasks and complete the schedule in the allocated time.

questions.e: Organizing a planning session with the development team allows for accurate estimation of tasks based on the team's knowledge and expertise. This collaborative approach ensures that the project schedule is realistic and achievable, taking into account the actual availability and capacity of the team members. By involving the development team in the estimation process, the project manager can create a more reliable project schedule and address the issue of developer availability effectively.

questions.q: During the course of a project, the project manager wants to ensure that the work carried out and the product being created do not deviate from the prescribed business value. What should the project manager pay special attention to in order to achieve this goal? *

o.t: Reviewing and updating the requirements management plan.
Carrying out quality audits and failure analyses.
Monitoring the work breakdown structure (WBS).
Monitoring and updating the benefits realization plan.

questions.e: Monitoring and updating the benefits realization plan ensures that the project continues to deliver the expected business value. The benefits realization plan tracks whether the project's outcomes are meeting the anticipated benefits and allows the project manager to make adjustments as necessary to stay aligned with the business objectives. This focus helps in maintaining the project's value proposition and ensures that the work being carried out remains relevant to the organization's strategic goals.

questions.q: During the design phase, a project manager realizes that the project will benefit from using adaptive tools. The effectiveness of this approach has been proven in past projects inside the organization. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Update project documents to include adaptive tools and artifacts and plan the first iterative session.
Contact the project sponsor and request new team members who are familiar with adaptive projects.
Confirm team capabilities before introducing adaptive tools and artifacts to the project.
Freeze the design stage and look for an external resource to run iterative design at extra cost.

questions.e: Before introducing adaptive tools and artifacts to the project, the project manager should first confirm that the team has the necessary capabilities and skills to effectively use these tools. If the team lacks experience with adaptive tools, they may need training or additional resources to ensure successful implementation. This step helps mitigate risks associated with adopting new methodologies and ensures the team can effectively leverage the benefits of adaptive approaches.

questions.q: A team is working on implementing a communications system when the client says that they are considering closing the project. The project manager schedules an urgent meeting with the client to understand why the project is at risk. Which two tools or techniques can the project manager use to influence the client’s decision to keep the project active? (Choose two) *

o.t: Alternatives analysis
Voting
Cost-benefit analysis
Multi-criteria decision making
Autocratic decision making

questions.e: Alternatives analysis: This technique involves evaluating different alternatives or solutions to address a problem. In this case, the project manager can use alternatives analysis to present the client with viable options to move forward with the project, which could convince them to keep it active. Cost-benefit analysis: This is a powerful tool for evaluating the financial aspects of the project. It can help the project manager demonstrate the potential benefits of continuing the project versus the costs. By clearly showing the benefits, the project manager can influence the client’s decision.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project that is halfway through its execution phase and the quality standards of the deliverables were formally accepted. However, a government agency has recently i ntroduced new standards that may significantly impact the project. The deliverables must be changed to align with the new quality standards. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Set up a structured, independent processes to determine if project activities followed the standards.
Schedule training for the project team on the new regulations introduced by the government agency.
Evaluate the impact the new regulations will have on the product and submit a change request.
Update the lessons learned register and inform senior management of the new standards.

questions.e: When new regulations are introduced that impact the project's deliverables, the project manager should first evaluate the impact of these new regulations on the project. This includes assessing how the new standards will affect the project's scope, schedule, cost, and quality. Once the impact is understood, the project manager should submit a change request to formally document the necessary changes to align the deliverables with the new quality standards. This ensures that the project continues to comply with all relevant regulations and maintains the quality and compliance required by the government agency.

questions.q: A large project is affecting the neighborhood in which it is located. The neighbors are not satisfied with the project and their resistance to the project may affect the project deadline. What two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Send letters to the neighbors and ask them kindly not to disturb the project.
Set up a meeting with neighborhood representatives to win their cooperation.
Analyze the situation and find out what is causing the neighborhood's negative attitude.
Ask the customer to extend the project deadline to allow time for conflict resolution.
Ask the mayor of the city to use their authority to stop neighborhood resistance.

questions.e: B. Set up a meeting with neighborhood representatives to win their cooperation: This action fosters direct communication and collaboration with the affected stakeholders. Engaging with neighborhood representatives helps to understand their concerns and work towards mutually acceptable solutions. It also shows that the project manager values their input and is willing to address their issues. C. Analyze the situation and find out what is causing the neighborhood's negative attitude: Understanding the root cause of the neighborhood's dissatisfaction is crucial for resolving the conflict. By analyzing the situation, the project manager can identify specific concerns and develop targeted strategies to mitigate the impact of the project on the neighborhood, thereby reducing resistance and potentially aligning the project with community interests.

questions.q: The marketing team is transitioning to using hybrid approaches for their projects. The marketing director is not knowledgeable about hybrid methodologies and the project manager needs the director’s support as the marketing director is a key stakeholder. What should the project manager do to obtain the support? *

o.t: Ask the marketing director to participate in daily meetings.
Mentor the marketing director on hybrid approaches.
Ask the marketing team members to coach the director.
Tram the marketing team and keep the director informed.

questions.e: B. Mentor the marketing director on hybrid approaches: Directly mentoring the marketing director on hybrid methodologies ensures that the director gains a comprehensive understanding of these approaches. This method is more effective because it provides personalized guidance and allows for tailored discussions to address any specific concerns or questions the director may have. Building this understanding and knowledge helps secure the director’s support as a key stakeholder, ensuring alignment and commitment to the hybrid approach.

questions.q: A company is using a predictive approach for the development of a particular component as defined in the scope management plan. Due to regularly changing regulatory requirements, the development team has requested to utilize agile approaches. What should the project manager do about the development team's request? *

o.t: Escalate the request for additional financial resources.
Forward the request to the project management office (PMO) to amend the organizational process assets.
Ask the project sponsor to obtain approval for implementation of the new approach.
Analyze the requirements that will need to be addressed under the requested method.

questions.e: When the development team requests to switch to an agile approach due to regularly changing regulatory requirements, the project manager's first step should be to analyze the requirements that will need to be handled under the new agile approach. The manager needs to evaluate whether adopting agile practices will help meet the evolving needs of the project, especially in terms of flexibility and responsiveness to changes in regulations. This analysis should also include determining the impact on the project timeline, deliverables, scope, and any necessary adjustments to processes.

questions.q: A new regulation has been approved that will impact the deliverables in the fourth phase of the project. The delivery is following an iterative approach and is currently completing the second phase. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Consult with the project sponsor to discuss a cost increase.
Acquire approval for an exception to the implementation of the new regulation.
Get approval for the additional budget from the steering committee.
Meet with subject matter experts (SMEs) to assess the impact to objectives.

questions.e: Meet with subject matter experts (SMEs) to assess the impact to objectives: Before taking any further steps, the project manager should consult with SMEs to understand the specific impact of the new regulation on the project's deliverables, objectives, timeline, and budget. This assessment will provide the necessary information to determine how significant the changes are and what adjustments might be needed. With a clear understanding of the impact, the project manager can then make informed decisions and take appropriate actions, such as discussing cost increases or seeking additional budget if necessary.

questions.q: An agile project is in its eighth iteration out of 16. After the last iteration review, the team members receive feedback from the security department about regulations with which the project must comply. Which two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Ask the team members to analyze the impact of including this regulation.
Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this regulation.
Ask the product owner to include the requirements in the product backlog.
Ask the security department for details about regulations.
Ask the team members to include the requirements in the next iteration.

questions.e: C: The product owner is responsible for managing the product backlog in an Agile project. Including the new requirements in the backlog ensures that they will be considered and prioritized along with other tasks. D: This is necessary to ensure that the team understands the requirements fully and can implement them correctly.

questions.q: During the development of a product, the project manager observes conflicts between project stakeholders, resulting in deliverable and output approval delays. On which area should the project manager focus? *

o.t: Revisiting the project management plan to ensure deliverables are on time.
Increasing the frequency of project update meetings to keep stakeholders informed.
Revisiting the stakeholder engagement plan, focusing on specific overlooked stakeholders.
Reviewing the business case and identifying gaps within scope.

questions.e: Conflicts between stakeholders often arise due to miscommunication or a lack of engagement. By updating the stakeholder engagement plan, the project manager can ensure that all stakeholders' needs and concerns are addressed, which can help in resolving conflicts and avoiding delays in deliverable and output approvals.

questions.q: A project manager realizes that a project is becoming delayed because some key decisions are affected by contradicting views between the organization's senior management and external stakeholders. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the stakeholder register and ensure that communications are being followed in line with the communications management plan.
Isolate the project team from external factors such as senior management and stakeholders so that decisions can be made more quickly.
Review the remaining scope and rebaseline the project’s schedule to take into account delays in decision making.
Review the adequacy of the project's governance and ensure that an appropriate structure is in place.

questions.e: Project delays caused by conflicting views between senior management and external stakeholders indicate a governance issue. The project manager should ensure that there is a clear decision-making framework in place, with defined roles, responsibilities, and escalation processes to resolve conflicts efficiently. Proper governance helps in addressing disagreements and ensuring timely decision-making to keep the project on track.

questions.q: A major project is unable to access the US$12 million funding allocated for the project. This prevents the start of the procurement process and is already leading to costly delays. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Escalate to the project steering committee.
Invite the finance department to the next project demo.
Review the project requirements.
Use the currently available resources.

questions.e: Escalate to the project steering committee: The project manager should escalate the issue to the project steering committee, as they typically have the authority and influence to address major funding and financial issues. The steering committee can help resolve the funding blockage, facilitate access to the allocated funds, and provide guidance on how to proceed. Escalating the issue ensures that the appropriate level of authority is involved in resolving critical funding issues that are beyond the project manager's control.

questions.q: A project manager has two projects that are being executed at the same time. The duration of the critical project must be reduced, but the project manager does not have enough resources to achieve this goal . In addition, the schedule does not have activities that can be overlapped. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Analyze both projects to determine the most effective use of common resources.
Use resource optimization to justify requesting more resources for the critical project.
Provide schedule optimization training to the project teams to improve their skills.
Apply fast-tracking techniques to compress the schedule of the critical project.

questions.e: When faced with a lack of resources and the need to reduce the duration of a critical project, the project manager should analyze both projects to identify any opportunities for reallocating resources in a way that optimizes their use. This approach allows for a strategic assessment of resource utilization across both projects to ensure that the critical project receives the necessary support without compromising the other project.

questions.q: During the execution of a project within an operations function the project manager encounters scope changes and a delay in the delivery of critical tasks. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Communicate the concerns to the project management office (PMO) during the weekly project reports.
Call for a team meeting to decide if the changes should be included.
Initiate the change request to modify the scope and adjust the timelines.
Conduct an impact analysis and present the results to the steering committee for approval.

questions.e: When scope changes and delays in critical tasks occur, the project manager should first conduct an impact analysis to understand the effects on the project’s schedule, cost, and overall objectives. After completing the impact analysis, the results should be presented to the steering committee for approval. This ensures that informed decisions are made regarding how to handle the changes and delays, and appropriate adjustments can be made to the project plan.

questions.q: Two functional managers disagree on key features of one deliverable during the planning of a project. The project manager discovers that each manager included requirements that contradict each other. The functional managers do not want to meet with each other to find a solution. This situation has been escalated to the sponsor who requests a meeting with them. What strategy should the project manager use to resolve this conflict in the meeting? *

o.t: Explain to the managers that the contradicting requirements are being considered for implementation in the project.
Explain to the managers that only one of the two requirements can be implemented, and submit a change request.
Ensure that both managers understand the requirements and search for a solution that best satisfies this deliverable.
Request that the managers explain why each requirement must be implemented and decide by considering the cost and benefits.

questions.e: The project manager should facilitate a meeting where both functional managers clearly understand each other’s requirements. The goal is to collaboratively search for a solution that best satisfies the deliverable while considering the project's objectives. This approach promotes cooperation and ensures that the final solution is acceptable to both parties, thus resolving the conflict effectively.

questions.q: A new project manager is planning an information security project for a company that resides in different countries. What is the first step the project manager should take to gather customer requirements? *

o.t: Conduct a stakeholder analysis to identify how regional policies may influence needs.
Request relevant stakeholders to conduct an analysis and reach consensus independently.
Conduct a project scope review workshop with relevant stakeholders.
Conduct project planning meetings in one location with relevant stakeholders.

questions.e: The first step in gathering customer requirements for a project that spans multiple countries is to conduct a stakeholder analysis. This will help identify and understand how regional policies and regulations may influence the stakeholders' needs and requirements. By doing this, the project manager can ensure that all relevant factors are considered and addressed in the project's planning and execution phases.

questions.q: An organization uses a hybrid approach to project management. A project manager has been assigned to an external project, project A, where two of the three modules in the project require machine learning skills. The only machine learning expert in the project manager's organization is engaged in an internal project, project B, that is about to end. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Prioritize project A over project B since A is an external project and B is an internal project.
Plan project A in sprints, starting with the module that does not require machine learning skills.
Engage the human resource manager to employ a machine learning expert for project A.
Plan project A to start at the end of project B when the machine learning expert is available.

questions.e: By planning project A in sprints and starting with the module that does not require machine learning skills, the project manager can begin work on the project immediately while waiting for the machine learning expert to become available after project B ends. This approach ensures that project A progresses without unnecessary delays and optimizes the use of available resources.

questions.q: A project manager finished reviewing the project deliverables for the current iteration with the customer. A new key stakeholder who just joined the customer's team, complains that the results do not provide the capabilities the business anticipated. What should the project manager do to address this issue? *

o.t: Create a change request and update the scope management plan.
Conduct stakeholder identification and a project objectives review session.
Update the stakeholder list and fix the deliverables.
Update the project management plan and lessons learned.

questions.e: When a new key stakeholder joins and raises concerns about the project deliverables, it is important to conduct stakeholder identification to understand the new stakeholder’s expectations and influence. A project objectives review session will help ensure that all stakeholders, including the new one, have a clear understanding of the project's goals and anticipated capabilities. This approach allows for alignment and addresses any gaps in understanding or expectations.

questions.q: Five agile teams working together on a product recently performed release planning Midway through the project, each team showed that their progress was on track. When all of the teams integrated at the product level, many integration issues were observed. The overall product release progress declined with predictions showing the committed content will not be able to be accomplished. What should the project manager have done differently? *

o.t: Formed a separate quality assurance team to test all items coming from each team at the end of each sprint.
Performed a Scrum of Scrums on a regular basis to help the teams remove impediments.
Ensured frequent and continuous integration of work to obtain early feedback and continuous learning.
Arranged an online session on the integration concept and suggested tools to the teams.

questions.e: The situation describes a scenario where teams were making progress in their individual sprints, but integration issues arose when their work was combined at the product level. This suggests that the teams weren't integrating their work frequently enough, which led to issues when they finally attempted to integrate. Frequent and continuous integration would have allowed the teams to identify integration problems earlier in the process, rather than discovering them later when it was too late to make easy adjustments. By continuously integrating work and obtaining early feedback, teams can spot problems early, resolve them, and avoid the significant delays caused by these last-minute integration issues.

questions.q: During daily calls team members share task progress. One team member does not usually communicate many details and has critical tasks to be completed. All team members are located in different countries and critical work is about to start. Which two options will help the project manager in this situation? (Choose two) *

o.t: Encourage all team members to use a virtual workspace.
Ask the team to send emails with detailed task progress.
Talk to the team member about their engagement and take appropriate action.
Reassign the work to a resource who participates in the daily calls.
Report the team member’s poor performance to the functional manager.

questions.e: A. Encouraging all team members to use a virtual workspace can help in centralizing communication and task progress tracking. This ensures that all team members have access to up-to-date information and can collaborate more effectively, regardless of their locations. C. Talking to the team member about their engagement and taking appropriate action is crucial to address any underlying issues they may have with communication. This direct approach helps to understand their perspective and find a solution to improve their participation in daily calls.

questions.q: A project manager has taken over an existing project. According to the previous project manager, the project is on track and within budget. However, stakeholders are unhappy with the recent progress report since the metrics show that the project is delayed and the cost is higher than expected. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with the previous project manager.
Submit a change request to the change control board (CCB).
Schedule training for project team members.
Conduct an earned value analysis (EVA).

questions.e: Conducting an earned value analysis (EVA) will provide the project manager with a detailed and objective assessment of the project's performance in terms of schedule and cost. This analysis will help identify the true status of the project, compare it against the planned performance, and provide valuable insights into the project's progress. With this information, the project manager can address stakeholders' concerns accurately and take corrective actions if necessary.

questions.q: In the middle of an iteration a team member suggests a new method of doing things. The method provides no value to the end customer, however it may help the team to work more efficiently. The change may require several days of work to implement. How should the project manager respond to the suggestion? *

o.t: The change should be considered and immediately added to the product backlog.
The change should be considered and presented to the project sponsor for approval.
The change should be considered because it will help the team work more efficiently.
The change should not be considered because it adds no value to the end customer.

questions.e: Since the change does not provide value to the end customer and may require several days of work, it’s best not to prioritize this change during the iteration. The project manager should focus on delivering customer value and avoid making adjustments that don't directly contribute to that goal. If the change could improve efficiency in the future, it might be considered for a later time, after customer value is delivered.

questions.q: The change control board (CCB) rejects a change request submitted by a subject matter expert (SME). The SME refuses to accept this rejection and does not want to continue the project without the change. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Requested that the sponsor approve the change request first.
Assessed the change's overall impact to the project before submission.
Ensured that the change request was aligned with the project scope.
Submitted the change request directly to the CCB.

questions.e: To avoid such situations, the project manager should have assessed the overall impact of the change request on the project before submission. This assessment helps in understanding the implications of the change on the project's scope, schedule, cost, and quality. By doing so, the project manager can make a more informed decision about whether the change request should be submitted and can better communicate the rationale behind the decision to the SME and other stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager works with a global virtual team. The team is facing difficulty in communicating with each other and often misses important messages. This difficulty leads to missed deadlines. What should the project manager do to enhance project team effectiveness? *

o.t: Implement team colocation to improve communication.
Identify the root cause of communication issues.
Initiate daily communication of project progress.
Schedule a communications control board meeting.

questions.e: Before implementing solutions, the project manager should first identify the root cause of the communication issues. Understanding the specific reasons behind the difficulties will allow the project manager to address the actual problems more effectively. Once the root cause is identified, appropriate measures can be taken to enhance communication and improve team effectiveness.

questions.q: A new agile team is having trouble completing tasks. There are many disputes occurring in the team. What should the agile leader do in this situation? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the team's manager.
Remove some of the team members.
Review the roles and responsibilities document.
Develop working agreements with the team.

questions.e: Developing working agreements helps set clear expectations for behavior, communication, and collaboration within the team. It fosters a sense of mutual understanding and respect, which can help reduce disputes and improve the team's ability to complete tasks effectively.

questions.q: After a performance review, a team member approaches the project manager and asks for feedback. The project manager mentions anecdotal information about this team member being a positive team player and generally getting their work done on time, even though they have been late with work once or twice. The team member expresses frustration at not having better information included in the annual performance review. What should the project manager do to prevent this frustration going forward? *

o.t: Request the human resource (HR) department to provide the key performance indicators (KPls) that were defined for this project.
Set team performance goals and explain how the team receives the same performance scores.
Review the key performance indicators (KPIs) for this team member and remind the team member how they are determined.
Provide the team member with velocity tracking tools and explain how the team member can see and track performance.

questions.e: Providing clear, objective performance metrics such as KPIs helps team members understand how their performance is evaluated. This approach addresses the team member's need for specific, measurable feedback and sets clear expectations for performance going forward. This can prevent frustration by ensuring that performance reviews are based on well-defined criteria

questions.q: A product owner has an idea for a new product but is struggling to define the features because they are not certain of the perceived business value for each feature. What should the project manager have the delivery team do to address this issue? *

o.t: Assess the product roadmap to see if there is another product that is more suitable for the build.
Develop a minimum viable product (MVP) for assessment from a select customer group.
Commission a business analyst to research similar competitor products.
Complete a work breakdown structure (WBS) to assess the cost of each feature.

questions.e: Developing a minimum viable product (MVP) allows the team to build and release a simplified version of the product that includes only the most essential features. This approach helps gather feedback from a select customer group to validate the perceived business value of each feature. By doing this, the product owner can make informed decisions about which features to prioritize based on real customer insights.

questions.q: A company has a lot of experience with predictive projects. The project management office (PMO) has been trying to implement iterative tools within the project management framework, and the project manager has been asked to use these tools in their current project After the successful implementation of the iterative tools, the PMO asks the project manager to determine the benefits these tools brought to the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Prepare and submit a status report to the steering committee to update performance monitoring.
Determine the data to be monitored during the project as well as the expected performance and targets.
Update the communications management plan to consider performance review meetings with the project stakeholders.
Conduct reviews with stakeholders to discuss the potential benefits the approach may have to the project.

questions.e: Conducting reviews with stakeholders allows the project manager to gather feedback and insights on the benefits and impact of using iterative tools in the project. This collaborative approach ensures that all perspectives are considered, and the true value of the iterative tools can be assessed based on stakeholder experiences and observations.

questions.q: The project manager has initiated the project and the team's roles and responsibilities have been assigned. In preparation for the development of the project management plan, the project manager reviews lessons learned from previous projects and discovers that the same team has been missing delivery dates. What should the project manager do to ensure timely delivery? *

o.t: Ask the team leader to assign other resources.
Update the issue log.
Include this in the risk register.
Escalate the issue to the functional manager.

questions.e: Including the issue of missing delivery dates in the risk register allows the project manager to formally recognize it as a risk and develop appropriate risk responses and mitigation strategies. By documenting it in the risk register, the project manager can monitor the risk throughout the project and take proactive measures to ensure timely delivery.

questions.q: An operations manager continuously raises concerns about a project's benefits to the company. While some concerns are valid most of the time these concerns have caused delays in project meetings. How should the project manager handle this? *

o.t: Discuss the meeting delays with the director of operations and ask for support with the concerns.
Review the operations manager's concerns and ensure these concerns are addressed.
Escalate the concerns to the project sponsor and discuss options to address them.
Include the operations manager's concerns in the risk register and assign actions to mitigate the risks.

questions.e: By reviewing and addressing the operations manager's concerns, the project manager demonstrates a willingness to listen and respond to valid issues, potentially reducing future delays. This approach can help build trust and cooperation with the operations manager, ensuring that any legitimate concerns are integrated into the project planning and execution process.

questions.q: The project manager has observed that two team members have been arguing with each other openly at meetings. To push their ideas through, each team member individually spoke with the sponsor directly and made decisions without informing the project manager or other team members. What two actions should project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Ask the team members work it out themselves
Discuss this situation with other project managers and ask for advice
Reiterate ground rules at the next meeting and ensure that all team members are clear about these rules.
Address the behavioral issue with each team member
Discuss the behavior directly with their managers and request them to correct the behavior.

questions.e: C. Reiterating ground rules at the next meeting helps ensure that all team members are reminded of the expected behavior and the proper channels for decision-making and communication. This can help prevent future instances of similar behavior. D. Addressing the behavioral issue with each team member directly allows the project manager to provide feedback and discuss the impact of their actions. This helps in resolving conflicts and promoting a collaborative team environment.

questions.q: The CEO has authorized the development of a complex financial product for a company to provide greater future benefits. The budget has been acquired through financing with global investors who expect all risks to be identified as soon as possible. What should the project manager use to identify the risks? *

o.t: An analysis of shared risks between parties.
Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis.
Expert judgment.
A risk value assessment.

questions.e: A SWOT analysis is a comprehensive tool that helps identify internal and external factors that could impact the project. By analyzing strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, the project manager can identify potential risks early in the project. This method is particularly useful when dealing with complex projects and helps ensure that all potential risks are considered and documented.

questions.q: The product owner decides to launch a product after a couple of releases knowing that the minimum viable product (MVP) lacks some features. One of the key stakeholders the marketing vice president is not happy with the results and questioned the release decision. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Support the product owner's decision and seek better alignment with this stakeholder in order to avoid this type of issue in the future.
Coach the team on the decision-making process, assuming a risk-averse strategy towards product releasing.
Assume the responsibility for product releases making the final call on when something is ready for customer launch.
Escalate the issue to the sponsor questioning the authority of the key stakeholder regarding the product launch decision.

questions.e: Supporting the product owner's decision maintains the integrity of the established decision-making process within the agile framework. Seeking better alignment with the marketing vice president helps address their concerns and improves collaboration and communication. This approach ensures that similar issues are avoided in the future by fostering a more cohesive understanding of product release decisions among all stakeholders

questions.q: An agile team has been struggling to keep up with the planned pace, which is frequently resulting in sprint failures. What should the project manager do to help avoid this situation in the future? *

o.t: Switch to a Kanban approach, implementing features on a first-come, first-serve basis, fostering a sustainable pace.
Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly.
Ask the project sponsor to approve overtime to compensate for the lack of performance while adjusting the plan.
Replace junior team members with more experienced ones and negotiate the project scope to compensate for the budget gap.

questions.e: By reviewing the team's velocity over the past several sprints, the project manager can gain a realistic understanding of the team's capacity and adjust future sprint plans to match their actual performance. This helps set achievable goals, fosters a sustainable pace, and reduces the likelihood of sprint failures. Adjusting the plan based on historical data ensures that the team is not overcommitted and can deliver consistent results.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to a project and receives the project charter from the project management office (PMO). The document is very clear about customer requests. During Project Scope Management, some requirements seem to be different from the ones specified within the project charter. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Modify the baseline of the project for minor impact changes to the project scope.
Use a focus group and brainstorming sessions to gather more details about the project scope.
Register the changes in the configuration management plan and send it to the change control board (CCB).
Explain to the sponsor that these requests could endanger the schedule and cost of the project.

questions.e: By conducting focus groups and brainstorming sessions, the project manager can gather detailed input from stakeholders, clarify any discrepancies, and ensure that the project's scope is accurately defined and agreed upon. This approach facilitates better communication, helps align expectations, and ensures that all requirements are thoroughly understood before making any changes to the project plan.

questions.q: A senior management team member contacts an agile project lead and mentions that certain features the senior manager thought would be in the current release were not included. What should the agile project lead do? *

o.t: Assure the senior manager that these features will be queued up in the next sprint.
Meet with the team to understand why the senior manager’s features were not included.
Invite the senior manager to the next planning meeting.
Send the product roadmap to the senior manager.

questions.e: By inviting the senior manager to the next planning meeting, the agile project lead ensures that the senior manager is directly involved in the prioritization and planning process. This approach fosters better communication and alignment of expectations between the team and senior management, helping to prevent misunderstandings about feature inclusion in future releases.

questions.q: In a hybrid project, the customer decided on a major change for the project design. This change was approved and the impact on schedule and budget is known. The software team leader, who is supposed to develop the software, refuses to commit to delivery dates claiming that they work using an agile approach and cannot commit to a final delivery date. The hardware team depends on this software to develop their part of the product. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Add this risk to the risk register and monitor it according to the risk management plan.
Escalate this to higher management and ask for help to resolve the issue.
Impose the delivery dates on the software team leader and notify the functional manager about the situation.
Ask the software team leader to use a predictive approach and commit to a delivery date.

questions.e: In a hybrid project, it is important to recognize and address the risks associated with combining different methodologies. By adding the risk of the software team's refusal to commit to delivery dates to the risk register, the project manager can formally acknowledge the issue and monitor it according to the risk management plan. This approach ensures that the risk is tracked, and appropriate mitigation strategies are developed and implemented. Escalating the issue or imposing dates may not align with the agile principles and could lead to further conflicts.

questions.q: The customer is reviewing the new reporting system and informs the project manager that one of the components in the printing module is not complete. The project manager reviews the work breakdown structure (WBS) and confirms that the component Is included. What does the project manager need to do first? *

o.t: Raise a change request to immediately implement the printing module component.
Escalate this issue to the project sponsor immediately.
Ask the project team to conduct a quality audit of the printing module components.
Meet with the project team to understand the issue and define actions.

questions.e: The first step the project manager should take is to meet with the project team to understand why the component in the printing module is not complete, even though it is included in the work breakdown structure (WBS). This meeting will help identify the root cause of the issue and allow the project manager and team to define appropriate actions to address it. This approach ensures that the project manager has all the necessary information before taking further steps.

questions.q: In a time-critical construction project, a misunderstanding occurred between the supervisor and the technician. The misunderstanding turned into a major conflict and the technician has complained to the project manager that they cannot continue to work under the supervisor any longer. The supervisor cites the technicians poor performance as the reason for the conflict. How should the project manager resolve the problem? *

o.t: Talk to the supervisor to tone down their approach and attitude.
Provide a just-in-time training to the technician to improve their skill set.
Use a direct, collaborative approach with the technician and supervisor.
Replace the technician with a high performing resource as time is critical.

questions.e: In a time-critical project, resolving conflicts quickly and effectively is essential. Using a direct, collaborative approach allows the project manager to address the issues openly with both the technician and the supervisor, facilitating clear communication and mutual understanding. This approach helps to resolve misunderstandings, improve working relationships, and maintain project momentum without the need for drastic measures like replacing team members.

questions.q: A project manager has just taken over a project that is halfway through its schedule. In a brief meeting with the client’s key project team, the project manager receives several requests from a specific client team member who was not at the project team meeting. The requests for information seem to be for trivial information that was previously submitted in project documents. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Send an email to the client team member explaining that they have the information already.
Review the stakeholder register to gain insight into the expectations of that team member.
Inform the client project manager that they are sending too many trivial requests.
Update the project risk register to include potential delays in answering these requests.

questions.e: Reviewing the stakeholder register helps the project manager understand the specific expectations, communication preferences, and influence of the client team member making the requests. This approach ensures that the project manager can address the requests appropriately and determine if there is a need for additional communication or clarification to meet the stakeholder's needs effectively.

questions.q: While reviewing prototypes, the quality team found some deviations that do not affect the functionality but have the potential to be an issue in the future. To avoid major problems in the future, the team recommends corrective actions that will require additional funds. The project is already struggling to stay on budget and has even used some of the contingency reserves. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the product designer why the deviation was not considered in the design phase.
Report to the project sponsor that the product is working and the project is struggling with the budget.
Evaluate and initiate the change request process with the stakeholders.
Ask the quality team to discard the sample and test again with a new sample.

questions.e: When deviations are found that have the potential to become issues in the future, it is important to evaluate the impact and initiate the change request process. This involves discussing the necessary corrective actions and their implications with the stakeholders. By following the change control process, the project manager ensures that all changes are properly reviewed, approved, and documented, helping to manage the project's budget and scope effectively.

questions.q: The project manager of a hybrid project learns that a stakeholder has approached a team member directly to request a change. This change will impact the project in a significant way. The project manager should tell the stakeholder that the correct procedure for new requirements is to provide a request directly to whom? *

o.t: Product owner
Change control board (CCB)
Project sponsor
Project manager

questions.e: In a hybrid project (which combines Agile and traditional methodologies), any significant change that impacts the project must go through a formal change control process. The Change Control Board (CCB) is responsible for reviewing, approving, or rejecting change requests to ensure they align with project objectives, budget, and timeline. By directing the stakeholder to submit the request to the CCB, the project manager ensures: Proper evaluation of the impact on scope, cost, schedule, and risks. Stakeholder transparency and structured decision-making. Avoidance of scope creep or unapproved changes disrupting the project.

questions.q: During a retrospective meeting a project manager hears that stakeholders have been constantly complaining at iteration demos about product features not being delivered as requested. Which advice should the project manager give to the Product owner to ensure that product features are always delivered as requested? *

o.t: Include stakeholders during daily standup meetings to monitor progress.
Validate acceptance criteria with stakeholders prior to backlog refinement.
Avoid including stakeholders in iteration reviews.
Create a requirements traceability matrix and distribute it accordingly.

questions.e: Validating acceptance criteria with stakeholders prior to backlog refinement ensures that the product owner clearly understands the stakeholders' requirements and expectations. By doing so, the team can align their work with what stakeholders expect, reducing the chances of features being delivered incorrectly. This proactive approach helps to ensure that the features meet the agreed-upon criteria and reduces the likelihood of complaints during iteration demos.

questions.q: A company is developing a new product. During project planning, a stakeholder from the legal department does not attend any of the project meetings and is not interested in the product design. How should the project manager deal with this situation? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor and seek assistance.
Engage the project stakeholder and ensure all requirements are captured.
Review the stakeholder engagement plan and communication strategy.
Review the product requirements and update the stakeholder register.

questions.e: Reviewing the stakeholder engagement plan and communication strategy helps the project manager assess how stakeholders are being engaged and communicated with throughout the project. This review will identify gaps in the current approach and help to develop a strategy to involve the stakeholder from the legal department more effectively. By addressing the engagement and communication needs specific to the legal stakeholder, the project manager can ensure that all necessary legal requirements are captured and considered in the project planning and execution phases.

questions.q: A project manager invites the company CEO, sponsor, team members, and an external client representative to a meeting to review the project management plan. The project manager starts to present the budget but the CEO suddenly asks to end the meeting. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Reviewed the communications management plan before inviting an external client representative to the meeting.
Reviewed the cost management plan with internal participants and CEO prior to inviting an external client representative to the meeting.
Performed a root cause analysis with the external client representative and documented the findings in the lessons learned register.
Sent the presentation slides to internal participants first and then to the external client representative prior to the meeting.

questions.e: By reviewing the communications management plan, the project manager would ensure that the appropriate information is shared with the right audience at the right time. This could have helped avoid the situation where sensitive information, such as the budget, was presented in a meeting with an external client representative without prior alignment with internal stakeholders.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project which is approaching the end of the execution phase. A high-level stakeholder informs the project manager that a very important requirement was not included in the scope of the project, and that without that requirement the project will deliver no value. What is the first thing the project manager should do? *

o.t: Include the requirement into the project and schedule it as soon as possible.
Inform the project sponsor about the situation and request assistance.
Evaluate the impact that the inclusion of this new requirement will have on project performance.
Inform the stakeholder that it is impossible to add new requirements to an approved project scope.

questions.e: The first thing the project manager should do is to evaluate the impact of including the new requirement. This involves assessing how the change will affect the project scope, schedule, budget, and overall project performance. By understanding the impact, the project manager can make an informed decision on how to proceed and provide this information to stakeholders and the project sponsor to facilitate a discussion on the best course of action. This approach ensures that decisions are based on a clear understanding of the consequences and allows for proper change management procedures to be followed.

questions.q: An organization is introducing agile to its projects. During an informal discussion, the project manager learned that team members who are currently working on different teams are discussing how they would like to be together on the same team. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: The project manager should not allow resources to choose teams because the project manager assigns the resources based upon project needs.
The project manager should not allow resources to choose on which team they would like to work because they will always choose their favorite team.
The project manager should allow the resources to periodically choose on which team they would like to work.
The project manager should indicate that the team members have already been assigned to a team through workforce optimization.

questions.e: Empowerment and Self-Organization: Agile principles emphasize empowering teams and allowing them to self-organize. Allowing team members to choose their teams periodically fosters motivation and engagement. Team Dynamics: When team members have the opportunity to work with those they prefer, it can enhance team cohesion and productivity, leading to better project outcomes. Flexibility: Periodic selection allows for flexibility and ensures that team composition can adapt to changing project needs and personal preferences over time. Allowing team members to periodically choose their teams aligns with agile principles and can lead to higher motivation and better team performance.

questions.q: The project velocity has recently slipped, and a decision was made to skip testing to increase the momentum and bring the project back on track. What will the project manager need to focus on as a result of this decision? *

o.t: Increased bum rate
Increased cost
Increased technical debt
Decreased efficiency

questions.e: Skipping testing to increase project momentum can lead to increased technical debt. Technical debt refers to the future costs and additional rework that arise from taking shortcuts in software development, such as not testing thoroughly. This debt can accumulate and cause more significant issues down the line, requiring more effort to fix problems that could have been identified and resolved during the initial testing phase. Therefore, the project manager should focus on managing and mitigating the increased technical debt resulting from the decision to skip testing.

questions.q: A highly skilled team resource received a job offer and is leaving the project soon. What should the project manager do to maintain project performance while a new team member is being onboarded? *

o.t: Log a risk in the risk register and work with the new team member to mitigate it.
Motivate the new team member to perform.
Share project documents with the new team member.
Offer cross-training and mentoring to the new team member.

questions.e: To maintain project performance while a new team member is being onboarded, it is essential to ensure that the new member can quickly get up to speed and become productive. Cross-training and mentoring can help transfer knowledge and skills from the departing team member to the new one. This approach ensures that the new team member understands the project's context, tools, processes, and specific tasks they need to perform. It also provides support and guidance during the transition, reducing the impact on project performance.

questions.q: A project manager submits a version of the software that the project team created. During the review meeting, a team member informs the project manager of a recent regulation that requires a dual verification process in the software. However, the product sponsor strongly insists there should be no updates to the software. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Include the new requirement in the next iteration of the software without informing the sponsor.
Inform the team that the sponsor decided to reject any changes and release the software as is.
Release the software as is and start a new project to deliver the new requirements.
Collect the requirements of the regulation and follow the change control process.

questions.e: When a new regulation requires changes to the software, it is critical to ensure compliance. The project manager should collect the details of the new regulation and follow the formal change control process. This approach ensures that all stakeholders, including the sponsor, are informed about the regulation and its implications. It allows for a structured review and decision-making process, ensuring that the project remains compliant while addressing any concerns from the sponsor about making changes to the software.

questions.q: A project manager is appointed for the deployment of a new solution. The solution will be integrated into the environment by a third-party vendor. This vendor just announced a delay in delivering a key component, which will impact the project schedule. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ensure that relevant stakeholders and expectations are identified and assess the component delay.
Perform a detailed analysis of the release content for each component of the solution.
Propose a new design of the solution to replace the external component with an internal one.
Ask for expedited delivery of the component to mitigate the risk of schedule delays.

questions.e: The first step in managing the delay caused by the third-party vendor is to identify and assess the impact of the delay on the project. This includes understanding which stakeholders are affected and what their expectations are. By assessing the delay, the project manager can gather the necessary information to make informed decisions and communicate effectively with stakeholders about the potential impacts and any mitigation strategies. This approach ensures a clear understanding of the situation and sets the stage for further actions to address the delay.

questions.q: A project team is engaging a development team in another country to develop software. During progress reviews, the project manager identified completion date delays due to rework because there were different interpretations of the client's needs. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Set up a meeting with key stakeholders to clarify requirements.
Escalate to the project steering committee and request additional time.
Travel to the development team's office to push the schedule.
Create prototypes with the development team to confirm requirements.

questions.e: When different interpretations of the client's needs lead to delays and rework, it is essential to clarify the requirements to ensure all parties have a common understanding. Setting up a meeting with key stakeholders to clarify the requirements helps to eliminate misunderstandings and aligns everyone's expectations. This approach fosters clear communication, reduces the chances of further rework, and helps the development team to understand exactly what is needed, thus improving the project's chances of staying on track.

questions.q: During an iteration demo, a customer noticed an enhancement they would like to make to the product. What should the team do next? *

o.t: Refine and estimate the enhancement so the size is known.
Add it to the product backlog to be completed in the future.
Start working on the enhancement for the customer immediately.
Ask the product owner to prioritize the item with the customer.

questions.e: When a customer requests an enhancement during an iteration demo, it is important to involve the product owner, who is responsible for managing the product backlog and prioritizing work items. The product owner should discuss the enhancement with the customer to understand its importance and urgency. This ensures that the enhancement is appropriately prioritized within the overall scope of the project and aligns with the customer's business goals. Once prioritized, the team can then plan and schedule the enhancement accordingly.

questions.q: A project manager is responsible for building a bridge. The high-level elements of the project are handled using a predictive approach. The software responsible for retracting the bridge has been developed based on agile principles. During software development, the workflow is often interrupted by various delays or impediments due to lack of information. How should the project manager handle this situation? *

o.t: Apply lean manufacturing to limit the team’s work.
Increase retrospectives to deliver results fast.
Make work visible using kanban boards.
Incorporate small batches of work into the project.

questions.e: In agile development, especially when dealing with frequent delays or impediments due to a lack of information, making work visible using Kanban boards is an effective strategy. Here’s why: Visibility: Kanban boards make the workflow visible to everyone involved. This helps identify where bottlenecks and impediments are occurring. Focus: It allows team members to focus on completing tasks and reduces the chances of getting interrupted by making it clear what the priorities are. Continuous Improvement: By visualizing the flow of work, the team can continuously improve their processes and address issues as they arise. Using Kanban boards helps manage workflow efficiently and address interruptions and delays by providing a clear visual representation of work in progress, completed work, and bottlenecks.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a virtual team that is geographically dispersed. What should the project manager do to avoid uncertainty in the project due to different cultures? *

o.t: Start the project and add any uncertainty that arises to the risk register.
Dissolve the virtual team and build a colocated team.
